sections.title: Console commands
sections.content:
Reference of Prism's `db:*` commands: what each does, its arguments and options, its exit codes and examples. For their use in Symfony, see [Prism in Symfony](symfony.md).

The examples are real outputs of `bin/prism` on SQLite, with two entities (`Customer`, `Invoice`); only absolute paths were shortened. The SQL shown depends on the platform of the connection.

sections.title: Console commands › Running the commands › `bin/prism` and `prism.php`
Console commands › Running the commands › Common conventions
sections.content:
- **Exit codes**: `0` (`Command::SUCCESS`), `1` (`Command::FAILURE`: an error, a database out of sync, a failed lint), `2` (`Command::INVALID`: a missing or invalid option, or a destructive command run without `--force`).
- **Destructive commands**: nothing runs without `--force`; the command says what it would have done and returns `2`.
- **`prod` environment**: `db:migrations:migrate`, `db:migrations:execute` and `db:database:drop` ask for confirmation, unless `--no-interaction`.
- **Global options** of Symfony Console, valid everywhere: `--no-interaction` (`-n`), `--quiet` (`-q`), `--verbose` (`-v`), `--ansi` / `--no-ansi`, `--help` (`-h`).
- The tables and sequences prefixed with `prism_` belong to Prism (`prism_migration_versions`, `prism_audit_log`): no command drops them as "not mapped".

sections.title: Console commands › Database › `db:database:create`
sections.content:
Creates the database named in the URL of the connection. Under PostgreSQL, Prism connects to the `postgres` database to create it; under SQLite, it creates the file.

| Option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--if-not-exists` | | Do nothing if the database exists (exit code `0`) |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:database:create

 [ERROR] Database "/srv/app/var/app.db" already exists; pass --if-not-exists to accept it.

$ vendor/bin/prism db:database:create --if-not-exists
```

sections.title: Console commands › Database › `db:database:drop`
sections.content:
Drops the database of the connection, with all its data. Requires `--force`; in `prod`, also asks for confirmation.

| Option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--force` | `-f` | Drop the database |
| `--if-exists` | | Do nothing if the database does not exist (exit code `0`) |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:database:drop

 ! [CAUTION] This would drop the database "/srv/app/var/app.db" and all its data; nothing was done.
 !           Run with --force to drop it.

$ vendor/bin/prism db:database:drop --force --if-exists
```

sections.title: Console commands › Schema without migrations
sections.content: For development and tests: the database follows the mapping directly. In production, use migrations.

sections.title: Console commands › Schema without migrations › `db:schema:create`
sections.content:
Creates the tables, indexes, foreign keys and sequences of the mapping. Refuses if one of the tables already exists.

| Option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dump-sql` | | Show the SQL instead of running it |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:schema:create --dump-sql

 [ERROR] These tables already exist: customer, invoice.
         Run db:schema:update to bring an existing database in line with the mapping.
```

sections.title: Console commands › Schema without migrations › `db:schema:update`
sections.content:
Brings the schema of the database in line with the mapping. Without `--force`, nothing runs: the command counts the statements and returns `2`. Tables that are not mapped are dropped only with `--complete`.

| Option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dump-sql` | | Show the SQL that would run |
| `--force` | `-f` | Run the SQL |
| `--complete` | | Also drop the tables and sequences that are not mapped (except `prism_*`) |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:schema:update --dump-sql
$ vendor/bin/prism db:schema:update --force
$ vendor/bin/prism db:schema:update --dump-sql

 [OK] Nothing to update: the database is in sync with the mapping.
```

sections.title: Console commands › Schema without migrations › `db:schema:drop`
sections.content:
Drops the tables and sequences of the mapping, and their data. Requires `--force`.

| Option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dump-sql` | | Show the SQL instead of running it |
| `--force` | `-f` | Run the SQL (destroys the data of the mapped tables) |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:schema:drop

 ! [CAUTION] This drops 2 table(s) and all their data: customer, invoice.
 !           Run with --force to execute, or --dump-sql to see the SQL.
```

sections.title: Console commands › Schema without migrations › `db:schema:validate`
sections.content:
Validates the mapping, then checks that the database matches it. Returns `1` if the mapping is invalid or the database is out of sync; warnings do not fail.

| Option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--skip-sync` | | Validate the mapping only, without connecting to the database |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:schema:validate

Mapping
-------

 [OK] The mapping of 2 entities is valid.

Database
--------

 [ERROR] The database is not in sync with the mapping: 4 queries pending. Run db:schema:update
         --dump-sql to see them.
```

sections.title: Console commands › Migrations
sections.content: A migration is a list of portable schema operations: the same migration runs on the four databases, and its SQL is produced by the platform when it runs. The files are named `VersionYYYYMMDDHHMMSS` and run in that order; their state is kept in the `prism_migration_versions` table. See the [migrations guide](/guide/migrations).

sections.title: Console commands › Migrations › `db:migrations:generate`
sections.content:
Creates an empty migration to fill in. With `--data`, a data migration (`VersionYYYYMMDDHHMMSSData`), which receives the entity manager and runs after the schema migration of the same version.

| Option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--data` | | Create a data migration |
| `--for` | | With `--data`: the schema migration it follows (`VersionYYYYMMDDHHMMSS`); a new version otherwise |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:migrations:generate --data --for=Version20261021205005

 [OK] Migration Version20261021205005Data created:
      migrations/Version20261021205005Data.php
```

Two migrations generated within the same second would have the same name: the command then refuses to overwrite the file and asks you to wait a second.

sections.title: Console commands › Migrations › `db:migrations:diff`
Console commands › Migrations › `db:migrations:migrate`
sections.content:
Runs the pending migrations, or migrates to a version: the pending migrations up to it, then the migrations executed after it, reverted from the newest to the oldest. `0` reverts everything.

- A migration modified after it ran blocks the command, unless `--allow-modified`: Prism keeps a checksum of the operations of each executed migration.
- A migration runs in a transaction when the platform can roll its DDL back (PostgreSQL). Otherwise, the command says so before it starts: a failure can leave the database half-migrated.
- In `prod`, the command asks for confirmation, unless `--no-interaction`.

| Argument / option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<version>` | | Target version (`VersionYYYYMMDDHHMMSS`), or `0` to revert everything; optional |
| `--dry-run` | | Show the SQL of each migration without running it |
| `--allow-modified` | | Run even if an executed migration was modified since |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:migrations:migrate --dry-run
 up   Version20261021204946 (without transaction)
      CREATE TABLE "customer" ("id" INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, "name" VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL, "email" VARCHAR(180) NOT NULL);
      CREATE TABLE "invoice" ("id" INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, "total" NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL, "customer_id" INTEGER NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT "fk_invoice_b335a48f" FOREIGN KEY ("customer_id") REFERENCES "customer" ("id") ON DELETE RESTRICT);
      CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "uniq_customer_45b166be" ON "customer" ("email");
      CREATE INDEX "idx_invoice_b335a48f" ON "invoice" ("customer_id");

 [WARNING] 1 migration(s) will run without a transaction: if one fails, the statements before the
           failure stay applied and the database is left half-migrated (RG-06.6).

 [OK] Dry run: 1 migration(s) planned, nothing executed.

$ vendor/bin/prism db:migrations:migrate --no-interaction
 up   Version20261021204946 (without transaction)
 ✔ up   Version20261021204946 (22 ms)

 [OK] 1 migration(s) executed in 22 ms.

$ vendor/bin/prism db:migrations:migrate 0 --dry-run
 down Version20261021204946 (without transaction)
      DROP TABLE "customer";
      DROP TABLE "invoice";
```

sections.title: Console commands › Migrations › `db:migrations:execute`
sections.content:
Runs one migration, in one direction: exactly one of `--up` and `--down` (exit code `2` otherwise). This is how a schema migration runs without its data migration. Asks for confirmation in `prod`.

| Argument / option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<version>` | | The version to run (`VersionYYYYMMDDHHMMSS`); required |
| `--up` | | Run its `up()` |
| `--down` | | Run its `down()` |
| `--dry-run` | | Show its SQL without running it |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:migrations:execute Version20261021204946 --down --dry-run
 down Version20261021204946 (without transaction)
      DROP TABLE "customer";
      DROP TABLE "invoice";

 [OK] Dry run: nothing executed.
```

sections.title: Console commands › Migrations › `db:migrations:status`
sections.content:
Sums up the position of the database: current version, latest version, number of executed and pending migrations. Reports a migration modified after it ran (which `migrate` will refuse) or whose file has gone.

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:migrations:status
 ----------------- -----------------------
  Directory         migrations
  Namespace         App\Migrations
  Current version   0
  Latest version    Version20261021204946
  Executed          0
  Pending           1
 ----------------- -----------------------
```

sections.title: Console commands › Migrations › `db:migrations:list`
sections.content:
Lists each migration with its state (`pending`, `executed`, `modified`, `missing`), its execution date in UTC, its duration and its description.

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:migrations:list
 ----------------------- ---------- --------------------- ---------- -------------
  Version                 State      Executed at (UTC)     Duration   Description
 ----------------------- ---------- --------------------- ---------- -------------
  Version20261021204946   executed   2026-10-21 20:49:47   22 ms
 ----------------------- ---------- --------------------- ---------- -------------
```

sections.title: Console commands › Migrations › `db:migrations:lint`
sections.content:
Analyzes the pending migrations before they run: their operations, applied one by one to the schema, checked against the data of the database, the mapping and the platform. An error fails the command (exit code `1`); a warning too with `--strict`. `#[IgnoreLint('L12', reason: '...')]` on a migration silences a rule you accept.

| Argument / option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<version>` | | Lint the pending migrations up to this version; optional |
| `--strict` | | Also fail on warnings |

| Code | Severity | Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L00 | error | Operation impossible on the schema |
| L01 | error | `NOT NULL` column without a default added to a table with rows |
| L02 | error | Column made `NOT NULL` while it holds `NULL`s |
| L03 | error | Column dropped while still mapped |
| L04 | error | Table dropped while still mapped |
| L05 | error | Table or column renamed while its old name is still mapped |
| L06 | error | Table dropped while a foreign key still references it |
| L07 | error | Unique index on duplicates |
| L08 | error | Foreign key on orphan rows |
| L09 | warning | Index without `CONCURRENTLY` on a table with rows, under PostgreSQL |
| L10 | warning | DDL on a table of more than a million rows, under MySQL and MariaDB |
| L11 | warning | Table with rows dropped |
| L12 | warning | Column dropped from a table with rows |
| L13 | warning | Column shrunk on a table with rows |
| L14 | warning | Column type changed on a table with rows |
| L15 | warning | Primary key changed on a table with rows |
| L16 | warning | Raw SQL (`$m->sql()`), neither portable nor analyzable |
| L17 | warning | Several DDL statements without a transaction, under MySQL and MariaDB |
| L18 | warning | Table created without a primary key |
| L19 | warning | Irreversible migration |
| L20 | warning | Vector index created on a table with rows: the HNSW graph is built over them |
| L21 | warning | Vector index on a `#[Tenanted]` table where one tenant, among others, has more than 10,000 rows, on MariaDB: a `nearest()` filtered by that tenant often falls back to an exact search over its rows |

sections.title: Console commands › Migrations › `db:migrations:lint`
sections.content:
```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:migrations:lint
 ----------------------- ------ ---------- ------------------------------------------------------
  Version                 Code   Severity   Message
 ----------------------- ------ ---------- ------------------------------------------------------
  Version20261021205005   L01    error      customer.full_name is added NOT NULL without a default
                                            to a table with rows: the existing rows have no value
                                            for it. Add it nullable, fill it, then make it NOT
                                            NULL; or give it a default.
  Version20261021205005   L12    warning    customer.name is dropped from a table with rows: its
                                            data is lost.
  Version20261021205005   L01    error      invoice.issued_at is added NOT NULL without a default
                                            to a table with rows: […]
 ----------------------- ------ ---------- ------------------------------------------------------

 [ERROR] 1 pending migration(s) linted: 2 error(s), 1 warning(s).
```

sections.title: Console commands › Mapping and tools › `db:mapping:info`
sections.content:
Lists the mapped entities, with their table and their repository.

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:mapping:info
 --------------------- ---------- ------------
  Entity                Table      Repository
 --------------------- ---------- ------------
  App\Entity\Customer   customer   -
  App\Entity\Invoice    invoice    -
 --------------------- ---------- ------------

 [OK] 2 mapped entities.
```

sections.title: Console commands › Mapping and tools › `db:query:sql`
sections.content:
Runs a raw SQL query, with bound named parameters (`:name`), never concatenated. A query that is not a read requires `--force` (exit code `2` otherwise).

| Argument / option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<sql>` | | The query, with `:named` parameters; required |
| `--param` | `-p` | A bound parameter, `name=value`; repeatable |
| `--force` | `-f` | Run a query that is not a read |
| `--max-rows` | | Maximum number of rows shown (default: 100) |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:query:sql "SELECT version, execution_time_ms FROM prism_migration_versions"
 ----------------------- -------------------
  version                 execution_time_ms
 ----------------------- -------------------
  Version20261021204946   22
 ----------------------- -------------------

 1 row(s).

$ vendor/bin/prism db:query:sql "DELETE FROM invoice"

 ! [CAUTION] This query is not a read: nothing was executed. Run with --force to execute it.

$ vendor/bin/prism db:query:sql --force "INSERT INTO customer (name, email) VALUES (:n, :e)" -p n=Ada -p e=ada@example.test

 [OK] 1 row(s) affected.
```

sections.title: Console commands › Mapping and tools › `db:import`
Console commands › Mapping and tools › `db:metamodel:generate`
sections.content:
Generates the metamodel classes of the typed query builder (`Customer_`, `Invoice_`...), and the IDE helpers. Only the files that change are rewritten; those of removed entities are deleted. The generated files are not versioned.

| Option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dir` | | Directory of the generated classes (default: `metamodelDir` of `PrismConfig`, `var/cache/prism/metamodel`) |
| `--ide-stub` | | Stub of the metamodel for IDEs, outside the directories they exclude (default: `.prism/metamodel.php`, to ignore in git) |
| `--phpstorm-meta` | | Directory of the PhpStorm metadata, where `prism.php` maps each entity to its repository (default: `.phpstorm.meta.php`) |
| `--no-ide` | | Generate the metamodel only, without the IDE helpers |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:metamodel:generate --no-ide
 written   App/Entity/Customer_.php
 written   App/Entity/Invoice_.php

 [OK] Metamodel in var/cache/prism/metamodel: 2 written, 0 unchanged, 0 deleted.
```

sections.title: Console commands › Mapping and tools › `db:cache:clear-metadata`
sections.content:
Clears the PSR-6 cache of the metadata, if there is one. Without a configured cache, the attributes are read on each run: there is nothing to clear.

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:cache:clear-metadata

 ! [NOTE] No metadata cache is configured: the attributes are read on each run, there is nothing to
 !        clear.
```

sections.title: Console commands › Mapping and tools › `db:audit:purge`
sections.content:
Deletes the rows of the audit log (`prism_audit_log`) older than the retention of their entity, `#[Prism\Auditable(retention: 'P10Y')]`. It is the only way to delete an audit row (GDPR). An entity without a retention is purged only with `--older-than`. Without `--force`, the command shows what it would delete.

| Option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--older-than` | | ISO 8601 retention for the audited entities that declare none, for example `P1Y` |
| `--force` | `-f` | Delete the rows |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:audit:purge --older-than=P1Y

 ------------------ ----------- --------------------- ------
  Entity             Retention   Rows before           Rows
 ------------------ ----------- --------------------- ------
  App\Entity\Order   P1Y         2025-10-26 09:00:00   1240
 ------------------ ----------- --------------------- ------

 ! [CAUTION] This would delete 1240 audit log row(s); nothing was done. Run with --force to delete them.

$ vendor/bin/prism db:audit:purge --older-than=P1Y --force
```

sections.title: Console commands › Embeddings
sections.content: An `#[EmbeddedVector]` field becomes stale when one of its source fields changes. A stale vector is left out of `nearest()` until it is computed again. Without a scheduler (the default), these commands compute the stale vectors. Like every `db:*` command, they see all the tenants.

sections.title: Console commands › Embeddings › `db:embeddings:compute`
sections.content:
Computes the stale vectors of every `#[EmbeddedVector]` field, or of one entity. It reads the source texts, calls the provider named by the attribute (`model: 'default'`), then writes each vector in a short transaction. A row whose source changed in the meantime stays stale: its own computation is already scheduled. If the provider fails, the command stops with exit code `1` and the remaining rows stay stale.

| Option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--class` | | Only this entity, by its class name or its short name |
| `--batch-size` | | Texts sent to the provider per call (default: `64`) |
| `--all` | | Also compute the vectors that are up to date, for example after changing the provider without a migration |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:embeddings:compute --class=Document
App\Entity\Document::$embedding: 1240 vector(s) computed.

 [OK] 1240 vector(s) computed.
```

sections.title: Console commands › Embeddings › `db:embeddings:status`
sections.content:
Counts the vectors of each `#[EmbeddedVector]` field: up to date, stale, and rows by model. `(none)` counts the rows that were never computed, or whose vector the application set itself.

| Option | Shortcut | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--class` | | Only this entity, by its class name or its short name |

```console
$ vendor/bin/prism db:embeddings:status

 ------------------------------- ------------ ------- ----------------------------------------------
  Field                           Up to date   Stale   Rows by model
 ------------------------------- ------------ ------- ----------------------------------------------
  App\Entity\Document::$embedding   1238         2       (none): 2, ollama/nomic-embed-text:v1.5: 1238
 ------------------------------- ------------ ------- ----------------------------------------------

 ! [NOTE] 2 stale vector(s): they are left out of nearest() until db:embeddings:compute (or the
 !        ComputeEmbedding messages) computes them.
```

To change the embedding model, a data migration marks every vector stale, then this command, or the messages, compute them again:

```php no-run
public function run(EntityManagerInterface $em): void
{
    $em->getRepository(Document::class)->markEmbeddingsStale('embedding');
}
```

sections.title: Prism in Symfony
sections.content: The `prism-orm/bundle` package replaces Doctrine in a Symfony 7.4 or 8 application: configuration, services, controllers, console, profiler, Messenger, Security and tests. Every example comes from Prism's demo application, a small ERP written with Prism alone.

sections.title: Prism in Symfony › Install
sections.content:
```bash
composer require prism-orm/bundle
composer require --dev symfony/maker-bundle prism-orm/test-pack
```

With Flex and the Prism recipe, the bundle is registered, `config/packages/prism.yaml`, `src/Entity/` and `migrations/` are created, and `DATABASE_URL` is added to `.env`. Without the recipe, add `Prism\Bundle\PrismBundle::class => ['all' => true]` to `config/bundles.php`: without a `prism.yaml`, Prism reads `DATABASE_URL` and maps `src/Entity/`.

The URL follows Symfony's format, and `serverVersion` is required:

```dotenv
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://app:!ChangeMe!@127.0.0.1:5432/app?serverVersion=16"
DATABASE_URL="mysql://app:!ChangeMe!@127.0.0.1:3306/app?serverVersion=8.4"
DATABASE_URL="mysql://app:!ChangeMe!@127.0.0.1:3306/app?serverVersion=11.8.0-MariaDB"
DATABASE_URL="sqlite:///%kernel.project_dir%/var/app.db?serverVersion=3.46.0"
```

sections.title: Prism in Symfony › Configure
sections.content:
One database, the short form:

```yaml
# config/packages/prism.yaml
prism:
    url: '%env(resolve:DATABASE_URL)%'
    entity_dirs: ['%kernel.project_dir%/src/Entity']
    migrations:
        dir: '%kernel.project_dir%/migrations'
        namespace: 'App\Migrations'
```

Several databases: named connections and entity managers, the first declared being the default one. Each entity manager has its own migrations (`migrations/Billing` and `App\Migrations\Billing` by default):

```yaml
prism:
    connections:
        default: { url: '%env(resolve:DATABASE_URL)%' }
        billing: { url: '%env(resolve:BILLING_DATABASE_URL)%' }
    entity_managers:
        default: { entity_dirs: ['%kernel.project_dir%/src/Entity'] }
        billing: { entity_dirs: ['%kernel.project_dir%/src/Billing/Entity'], batch_size: 50 }
```

| Option | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity_managers.*.connection` | the connection with the same name, or the only one | The connection of the entity manager |
| `entity_managers.*.batch_size` | `100` | The batch size of [batch fetching](/guide/n-plus-one#batch-size) |
| `default_entity_manager` | the first declared | The one behind `EntityManagerInterface` |
| `connection_idle_ttl` | `60` | Worker mode: seconds of inactivity before the connection is checked (`0`: on every request) |
| `metamodel.dir` | `%kernel.cache_dir%/prism/metamodel` | Where the metamodel is generated, one subdirectory per entity manager |
| `tenancy` | | [Multi-tenancy](/guide/multi-tenancy#in-symfony) |

An unknown option is refused when the container compiles, with a message that names it.

sections.title: Prism in Symfony › Create entities
sections.content:
```bash
bin/console make:entity Order
```

`make:entity` creates the entity and its repository, then adds fields and relations one by one. For a relation, it offers the inverse side and writes both sides (`inversedBy`, `mappedBy`); a collection is initialized in the constructor. On an existing entity, it only adds the new members: your code and comments are kept. The metamodel is regenerated on the next request. Next to DoctrineBundle, during a migration from Doctrine, the commands are named `make:prism:entity` and `make:prism:migration`.

The mapping itself is described in [Mapping entities](/guide/mapping).

sections.title: Prism in Symfony › Migrations
sections.content:
```bash
bin/console make:migration            # or db:migrations:diff
bin/console db:migrations:lint        # dangerous operations (19 rules)
bin/console db:migrations:migrate
```

With several entity managers, every `db:*` command takes `--em=billing`. See [Migrations](/guide/migrations).

Prism in Symfony › Validation and security
sections.content:
The `#[UniqueEntity]` constraint checks uniqueness with the right entity manager, on fields and relations:

```php
#[Prism\Entity]
#[UniqueEntity(fields: ['number'])]
final class CreditNote
{
    #[Prism\Id, Prism\GeneratedValue]
    public ?int $id = null;

    #[Prism\Column(length: 20, unique: true)]
    public string $number;
}
```

The `prism` user provider loads users from an entity:

```yaml
# config/packages/security.yaml
security:
    providers:
        users:
            prism: { class: App\Entity\User, property: email }
```

Without `property`, the repository implements `Prism\Bundle\Security\UserLoaderInterface`. A password hash is upgraded by the repository if it implements `PasswordUpgraderInterface`.

sections.title: Prism in Symfony › Profiler
sections.content:
In development, the Prism panel shows the queries and their duration, the **N+1 queries detected, with the line of your code that caused them**, the batch loads, and the changeset of each flush. The **Tenant** and **Audit** panels show the tenant of the request and the audit rows it wrote. Query recording stops at 1,000 queries per request.

In production, neither the panels, nor the query recording, nor the N+1 detector exist in the container.

sections.title: Prism in Symfony › Worker mode and Messenger
sections.content:
Under FrankenPHP or RoadRunner, there is nothing to do: between two requests, the entity managers are cleared, a transaction left open is rolled back, the tenant is forgotten, and a lost connection is reconnected at the start of the next request, never in the middle of a transaction. The demo serves 10,000 requests from one worker without memory growth.

For Messenger, the `prism_reset` middleware does the same between two messages:

```yaml
framework:
    messenger:
        buses:
            messenger.bus.default:
                middleware: [prism_reset]
```

sections.title: Prism in Symfony › Embeddings
sections.content:
An `#[EmbeddedVector]` field is computed from its source fields by an embedding provider, named by the attribute (`model: 'default'`). The bundle registers the providers by name:

```yaml
prism:
    embeddings:
        scheduler: auto        # messenger | synchronous | deferred
        batch_size: 64         # texts per provider call, ids per message
        providers:
            default:
                openai: { base_url: 'http://ollama:11434/v1', model: 'nomic-embed-text:v1.5', dimensions: 768 }
            legacy:
                service: App\Embedding\LegacyProvider
```

The `openai` form needs `composer require prism-orm/embedding-openai symfony/http-client`. It speaks the `/v1/embeddings` API of OpenAI, Mistral, Ollama, vLLM, LocalAI and Text Embeddings Inference; give `api_key` for a hosted one. Any service that implements `EmbeddingProvider` is also registered: under the name of its `#[AsEmbeddingProvider('name')]` attribute, or under its service id.

When a source field changes, the flush marks the vector stale; once the transaction is committed, the scheduler takes over:

- `messenger`: dispatches one `ComputeEmbedding` message per batch of ids. Route it to an asynchronous transport. The handler processes the messages in batches, in the tenant of the rows, and a failure is retried by Messenger. `auto` picks it when a message bus exists.
- `synchronous`: computes the vectors at once, after the flush. For scripts and small applications.
- `deferred`: does nothing; run `db:embeddings:compute`, by hand or from a cron. `auto` picks it without Messenger.

```yaml
framework:
    messenger:
        transports:
            async: '%env(MESSENGER_TRANSPORT_DSN)%'
        routing:
            Prism\Bundle\Messenger\ComputeEmbedding: async
```

A stale vector is left out of `nearest()` until it is computed again. At `cache:warmup`, an unknown provider name, or a provider whose dimension is not the one of the column, is refused with the other mapping errors.

Prism in Symfony › Known limitations
sections.content:
- A custom type converts its values, but cannot declare its column yet (`db:schema:create`).
- An entity manager accepts an entity of another entity manager and queries it in its own database. The controller argument resolver, `#[UniqueEntity]` and the test pack pick the right one.
- Vector and hybrid search arrive in Prism 0.9.

sections.title: Audit and behaviors
sections.content:
Business data needs to know when it changed, who changed it, and what it looked like before. Four class attributes cover this, with no extra package: `#[Prism\Timestampable]`, `#[Prism\Blameable]`, `#[Prism\SoftDeletable]` and `#[Prism\Auditable]`.

The examples run on the demo application, where `Order` is timestamped and blamed, `Customer` is soft-deletable and `Invoice` is audited.

Audit and behaviors › Soft delete
Audit and behaviors › Audit log
Audit and behaviors › Audit log › Reading the history
Audit and behaviors › Audit log › Append only
sections.content:
No Prism API updates or deletes an audit row. Old rows are removed by one command, according to the `retention` of each entity, an ISO 8601 duration:

```console
$ bin/console db:audit:purge                 # shows what would be deleted
$ bin/console db:audit:purge --force
$ bin/console db:audit:purge --older-than=P1Y --force   # for entities without a retention
```

Each audit row also publishes an `AuditRecordedEvent`, to copy the log elsewhere. In Symfony, the **Audit** panel of the profiler lists the rows written during the request.

sections.title: Audit and behaviors › Without Symfony
sections.content:
The clock, the author and the request identifier are arguments of the `EntityManager`:

```php no-run
return new EntityManager(
    $connection,
    $metadata,
    clock: $clock,                         // a PSR-20 ClockInterface; UTC system time by default
    actorProvider: $actorProvider,         // a Prism\Orm\Behavior\ActorProvider: getActor(): ?string
    requestIdProvider: $requestIdProvider, // a Prism\Orm\Audit\RequestIdProvider: getRequestId(): ?string
);
```

Without an `ActorProvider`, `createdBy`, `updatedBy` and the author of audit rows stay `null`.

sections.title: Working with entities
sections.content:
The `EntityManager` saves, loads and tracks your entities. Its unit of work remembers every entity it manages and, at `flush()`, writes what changed in one transaction.

The examples run on the demo application: `Customer`, `Order`, `OrderLine`, `Product` and `Invoice` entities, with Acme as the current tenant.

sections.title: Working with entities › Entity states
sections.content:
An entity is in one of four states:

| State | Meaning | Reached by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NEW` | Unknown to Prism | `new Customer()` |
| `MANAGED` | Tracked: its changes are written at the next flush | `persist()`, or loaded by Prism |
| `REMOVED` | Deleted at the next flush | `remove()` on a managed entity |
| `DETACHED` | No longer tracked | `detach()`, `clear()` |

Any other transition throws `InvalidEntityStateException`: for example, `remove()` on a new entity, or `persist()` on a detached one. A removed entity becomes managed again if you `persist()` it before the flush.

sections.title: Working with entities › Saving
Working with entities › Loading
sections.content:
```php
$customers = $em->getRepository(Customer::class);

$customer = $customers->findOneBy(['email' => 'customer1@acme.example.test']);
$same = $em->find(Customer::class, $customer->id);

var_dump($same === $customer); // bool(true)
```

The unit of work keeps an identity map: within one entity manager, one row is one object. `find()` returns the instance already loaded instead of querying again, until `clear()`.

The repository methods:

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `find($id)` | The entity, or `null` |
| `findOneBy($criteria, $orderBy)` | The first match, or `null` |
| `findBy($criteria, $orderBy, $limit, $offset)` | `list<T>` |
| `findAll()` | `list<T>` |
| `count($criteria)` | `int` |
| `iterate($criteria, $batchSize)` | A generator, for large result sets |

A criterion is an equality on a field; a list of values means `IN`, `null` means `IS NULL`. For anything else, use the [typed query builder](/guide/getting-started#query).

sections.title: Working with entities › References
sections.content:
When you only need an entity to point at it, a reference avoids a query:

```php
$customerId = $em->getRepository(Customer::class)->findOneBy(['email' => 'customer2@acme.example.test'])->id;
$em->clear();

$customer = $em->getReference(Customer::class, $customerId); // no query
echo $customer->id;                                         // still no query
echo $customer->name;                                       // loads the row
```

The reference is a PHP 8.4 lazy ghost: an object of the real class, whose identifier is readable without loading. Any other property access loads the row once. If the row does not exist anymore, that access throws `EntityNotFoundException`.

sections.content:
| Method | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `refresh($entity)` | Reads the row again; unsaved changes to the entity are lost |
| `detach($entity)` | Stops tracking the entity; its changes will not be saved |
| `clear()` | Detaches every entity and releases them: call it between two jobs in a long-running process |
| `contains($entity)` | Whether the entity is managed |

sections.title: Coming from Doctrine
sections.content: Prism keeps the concepts of Doctrine ORM: entities mapped with attributes, an `EntityManager` with `persist()` and `flush()`, a unit of work, repositories, lifecycle callbacks, migrations. Most of an application's code keeps its shape. What changes is the mapping syntax, the way queries are written, and a few rules that Prism enforces where Doctrine lets them go.

sections.title: Coming from Doctrine › An entity, side by side
Coming from Doctrine › Attributes
sections.content:
| Doctrine | Prism |
| --- | --- |
| `#[ORM\Entity]`, `#[ORM\Table]` | `#[Prism\Entity]`, `#[Prism\Table]` |
| `#[ORM\Id]`, `#[ORM\GeneratedValue]` | the same; `strategy: GenerationStrategy::UuidV7` for UUIDs |
| `#[ORM\Column(type: Types::...)]` | `#[Prism\Column(type: '...')]`, often deduced |
| `#[ORM\JoinColumn]`, `#[ORM\JoinColumns]` | `joinColumn:`, `onDelete:`, `foreignKey:` of the relation |
| `#[ORM\JoinTable]` | `#[Prism\JoinTable]` |
| `#[ORM\ManyToOne]`, `#[ORM\OneToMany]`, `#[ORM\OneToOne]`, `#[ORM\ManyToMany]` | the same names and parameters, `cascade` as enums |
| `#[ORM\OrderBy]` | `#[Prism\OrderBy]`, with `Prism\Dbal\Query\Order` cases |
| `#[ORM\Index]`, `#[ORM\UniqueConstraint]` | the same, on fields |
| `#[ORM\Embeddable]`, `#[ORM\Embedded]` | the same; a nullable embeddable is `null` when its columns are |
| `#[ORM\Version]` | `#[Prism\Version]` |
| `#[ORM\HasLifecycleCallbacks]`, `#[ORM\PrePersist]`... | the same names |
| `#[ORM\EntityListeners]` | `#[Prism\EntityListeners]` |
| `#[ORM\InheritanceType]`, `#[ORM\DiscriminatorMap]` | not supported in 1.0 |
| `#[ORM\Cache]` | not supported in 1.0 |

The [attribute reference](/reference/attributes) lists every parameter.

sections.title: Coming from Doctrine › Types
sections.content:
| Doctrine | Prism |
| --- | --- |
| `string`, `text`, `integer`, `bigint`, `smallint`, `boolean`, `float`, `json`, `binary` | the same |
| `decimal` | `decimal`, a `string` in PHP, as in Doctrine |
| `datetime_immutable`, `date_immutable`, `time_immutable` | the same |
| `datetime`, `date`, `time` (mutable) | refused: use `\DateTimeImmutable` |
| `guid` | `uuid` |
| `simple_array`, `array`, `object` | no equivalent: use `json` |
| `datetimetz_immutable` | no equivalent: store UTC dates |

Custom types extend `Prism\Dbal\Type\Type`.

sections.title: Coming from Doctrine › Repositories
Coming from Doctrine › Queries
sections.content:
DQL and its query builder are replaced by the typed query builder:

```php no-run [Doctrine]
$invoices = $em->createQueryBuilder()
    ->select('i')
    ->from(Invoice::class, 'i')
    ->join('i.order', 'o')
    ->where('i.paid = :paid')
    ->andWhere('o.status = :status')
    ->setParameter('paid', false)
    ->setParameter('status', 'shipped')
    ->orderBy('i.issuedAt', 'DESC')
    ->getQuery()
    ->getResult();
```

```php [Prism]
$i = Invoice_::as('i');
$o = $i->order->as('o');

$invoices = $em->query($i)
    ->join($o)
    ->where($i->paid->eq(false))
    ->andWhere($o->status->eq('shipped'))
    ->orderBy($i->issuedAt->desc())
    ->getResult();
```

The structure is the same; the strings are gone. `Invoice_` is generated from the entity: a renamed field breaks the queries that use it in PHPStan, not in production. `addSelect()` with a join becomes `fetchJoin()`; `NEW Dto(...)` becomes `selectInto(Dto::class, ...)`; Doctrine's `Paginator` becomes `paginate()`. See [Typed queries](/guide/query-builder).

There is no textual query language. For SQL that the builder does not cover, use the connection: `$em->getConnection()->executeQuery($sql, $params)`.

sections.title: Coming from Doctrine › Behaviors that change
sections.content:
- **N+1 queries.** Doctrine loads each lazy relation separately unless you join it; Prism loads it for every entity of the query at once. Loops that relied on `fetch: 'EAGER'` or on joins added for performance can be simplified. See [Avoiding N+1 queries](/guide/n-plus-one).
- **No proxies.** References are PHP 8.4 lazy ghosts: objects of the real class. `instanceof`, `::class` and `get_class()` give the entity class, never a proxy class.
- **The constructor is never called** when an entity is loaded, as in Doctrine. Derived state goes in `#[PostLoad]`.
- **Change detection compares database values**: an entity whose `\DateTimeImmutable` was replaced by an equal one is not updated.
- **A failed flush leaves the unit of work as it was before.** Doctrine closes the entity manager after a failure; Prism rolls back and lets you fix the cause and flush again.
- **Mutable dates are refused**, where Doctrine accepts them.

sections.content:
| Doctrine | Prism |
| --- | --- |
| `doctrine:database:create`, `drop` | `db:database:create`, `drop` |
| `doctrine:schema:create`, `update`, `drop`, `validate` | `db:schema:create`, `update`, `drop`, `validate` |
| `doctrine:migrations:diff`, `migrate`, `execute`, `status`, `list`, `generate` | `db:migrations:diff`, `migrate`, `execute`, `status`, `list`, `generate` |

Prism adds `db:migrations:lint`, which checks pending migrations against the data before they run.

sections.title: Coming from Doctrine › Migrating an application
sections.content:
1. **Install Prism next to Doctrine.** `composer require prism-orm/bundle`. Its services and commands have their own names (`Prism\Orm\EntityManagerInterface`, `db:*`, `make:prism:*`), so both bundles work side by side while you migrate. Point Prism at the same `DATABASE_URL`.
2. **Get Prism entities.** Either convert your entities' attributes with the tables above, or generate them from the database: `bin/console db:import --namespace='App\Entity' --dry-run`. `db:import` writes `final`, strictly typed entities with their relations, and reports what it approximates; it never overwrites a file without `--force`.
3. **Check the mapping against the database.** `bin/console db:migrations:diff --dry-run` must generate nothing: the entities describe the existing tables exactly. Prism keeps its own migration table, `prism_migration_versions`, and ignores `doctrine_migration_versions`; the existing Doctrine migrations stay in Doctrine's history.
4. **Port the repositories and queries**, one module at a time. PHPStan and the [extension](/guide/phpstan) find the wrong field names.
5. **Port the listeners and extensions** with the table above.
6. **Port the tests** to the test pack: factories, `ResetDatabase`, and `assertQueryCount()` to keep the query counts you gained.
7. **Remove Doctrine.** `composer remove doctrine/doctrine-bundle doctrine/orm`, and generate the next migrations with `db:migrations:diff`.

sections.title: Coming from Doctrine › Not supported
sections.content: Some Doctrine features have no equivalent in Prism 1.0, by design or by lack of time: entity inheritance (single table and class table), composite primary keys, DQL strings, XML and YAML mapping, the second-level cache, and `datetimetz` columns. Check that your model does not depend on them before you start.

For anything beyond equality, use the typed query builder. `Product_` is generated from your entity:

```php
$p = Product_::as('p');

$desks = $em->query($p)
    ->where($p->name->like('%desk%'))
    ->andWhere($p->price->lt('1000.00'))
    ->orderBy($p->price->asc())
    ->getResult(); // list<Product>
```

Each field knows its type: `$p->price->lt(1000)` is refused by PHPStan, because a decimal compares with a string. In Symfony, the metamodel is regenerated when an entity changes; without Symfony, run `vendor/bin/prism db:metamodel:generate`.

sections.title: Installation
sections.content: Prism needs PHP 8.4 or later with the PDO driver of your database (`pdo_mysql`, `pdo_pgsql` or `pdo_sqlite`). The supported database versions are listed in the [requirements](/guide/introduction#requirements).

sections.title: Installation › In a Symfony application
sections.content:
Prism replaces Doctrine in a Symfony 7.4 or 8 application:

```bash
composer require prism-orm/bundle
```

With Symfony Flex and the Prism recipe, this registers the bundle, creates `config/packages/prism.yaml`, the `src/Entity/` and `migrations/` directories, and adds `DATABASE_URL` to `.env`. Without the recipe, register the bundle yourself:

```php
// config/bundles.php
return [
    // ...
    Prism\Bundle\PrismBundle::class => ['all' => true],
];
```

Without a `prism.yaml` file, Prism reads `DATABASE_URL` and maps the entities of `src/Entity/`.

The development tools are separate packages:

```bash
composer require --dev symfony/maker-bundle prism-orm/test-pack
```

`symfony/maker-bundle` brings `make:entity` and `make:migration` for Prism, and `prism-orm/test-pack` the factories and database helpers for your tests.

Installation › The database URL
sections.content:
Prism reads the same URL format as Symfony. `serverVersion` is required: it selects the SQL dialect without connecting first.

```dotenv
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://app:!ChangeMe!@127.0.0.1:5432/app?serverVersion=16"
DATABASE_URL="mysql://app:!ChangeMe!@127.0.0.1:3306/app?serverVersion=8.4"
DATABASE_URL="mysql://app:!ChangeMe!@127.0.0.1:3306/app?serverVersion=11.8.0-MariaDB"
DATABASE_URL="sqlite:///%kernel.project_dir%/var/app.db?serverVersion=3.46.0"
```

Create the database if it does not exist yet:

```console [Symfony]
$ bin/console db:database:create
```

```console [Without Symfony]
$ vendor/bin/prism db:database:create
```

sections.content:
The PHPStan extension checks your queries and repository calls during analysis:

```bash
composer require --dev prism-orm/phpstan phpstan/extension-installer
```

```neon
parameters:

```

sections.title: What is Prism?
sections.content:
Prism is an object-relational mapper for PHP 8.4 and later. You describe your entities with PHP attributes; Prism creates the schema, loads and saves your objects, tracks what changed and writes it in one transaction.

It is built for business applications: ERPs, B2B software, back offices. These applications have many relations, many customers sharing one database, and amounts that must never be rounded. Prism handles each of these by default instead of leaving it to every developer.

sections.title: What is Prism? › Four pillars
sections.content:
**1. No N+1 queries.** Entities loaded by the same query form a *cohort*. When you initialize a lazy relation of one entity, Prism loads that relation for the whole cohort in one `WHERE id IN (...)` query. In development, a detector reports repeated queries with the file and line that triggered them, in the Symfony profiler.

**2. Typed queries.** Prism generates a metamodel class per entity (`Order_` for `Order`). Queries use its typed fields instead of strings, return `list<Order>`, and a PHPStan extension checks field names, value types and DTO projections before the code runs.

**3. Multi-tenancy and audit.** An entity marked `#[Tenanted]` gets a `tenant_id` column that Prism fills, filters and checks in every query, including lazy loading, batch fetching and raw SQL. `#[Auditable]`, `#[Timestampable]`, `#[Blameable]` and `#[SoftDeletable]` cover the rest of what business data needs.

**4. Vector and hybrid search.** A `vector` type for MariaDB and PostgreSQL (pgvector), HNSW and full-text indexes, `nearest()` and `hybridSearch()` on every repository, with the usual filters applied before the ranking. `#[EmbeddedVector]` keeps a vector in step with its text: stale at flush, recomputed after the commit by a provider you choose. See [Vector search](/guide/vector-search).

sections.title: What is Prism? › Design choices
sections.content:
- **Attributes only.** No XML, no YAML: the mapping lives next to the properties it describes.
- **No proxy classes.** Lazy relations use PHP 8.4 native lazy ghosts. Nothing is generated for your entities, which can be `final`, and `readonly` properties are supported.
- **Your constructor stays yours.** Prism never calls it when loading an entity; use `#[PostLoad]` to compute derived state.
- **Exact values.** A `decimal` column is always a PHP `string`, never a `float`. Dates are `\DateTimeImmutable`; a mutable `\DateTime` property is refused when the mapping is validated.
- **Atomic flush.** `flush()` runs in one transaction. If it fails, the transaction is rolled back and the unit of work is left exactly as it was before the flush.
- **Fail closed.** Without a current tenant, any operation on a tenanted entity throws. There is no implicit "all tenants" mode.
- **Safe migrations.** Migrations are generated from your entities, renames are detected and confirmed, a linter flags dangerous operations, and a migration modified after it ran blocks the next run.

sections.title: What is Prism? › Requirements
sections.content:
| | Supported | Tested in CI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHP | 8.4 and later | 8.4, 8.5 |
| MySQL | 8.0 and later | 8.4 |
| MariaDB | 11.8 and later | 11.8 |
| PostgreSQL | 15 and later | 16 |
| SQLite | 3.40 and later, for development and tests | |
| Symfony (optional) | 7.4 and 8 | 7.4, 8 |

sections.content: Some features are deliberately out of scope for the first stable version: a textual query language (the typed query builder replaces DQL), entity inheritance, composite primary keys, Oracle and SQL Server, and a second-level cache.

sections.title: What is Prism? › Project status
sections.content:
Prism is in its `0.x` series, one minor version per milestone, toward a 1.0 release. Until then, the public API may still change between minor versions; a change is announced by a deprecation one minor version before the removal. What changed in each version is listed in the [changelog](https://github.com/IMAMx39/prism/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

Every example on this site is executed in CI against the four supported databases, on the data of Prism's demo application: a small ERP with two companies (Acme and Globex), their customers, orders, invoices, and a shared product catalog.

sections.title: Mapping entities
sections.content:
The mapping tells Prism how a class is stored. It is written with PHP attributes on the class and its properties, and Prism deduces everything it can from the PHP types. The examples write the attributes with the `Prism\` alias:

```php no-run
use Prism\Orm\Mapping as Prism;
```

sections.title: Mapping entities › Entities and tables
Mapping entities › Identifiers
sections.content:
Every entity has exactly one identifier, marked `#[Prism\Id]`. Composite keys are not supported.

```php
#[Prism\Entity]
final class Shipment
{
    #[Prism\Id, Prism\GeneratedValue(Prism\GenerationStrategy::UuidV7)]
    #[Prism\Column(type: 'uuid')]
    public ?string $id = null;
}
```

`#[Prism\GeneratedValue]` chooses who generates it:

| Strategy | Column | Generated by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Auto` (default) | integer | `Identity` under MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite, `Sequence` under PostgreSQL |
| `Identity` | integer | The database, with an auto-increment column |
| `Sequence` | integer | A database sequence, named `<table>_id_seq` unless `sequenceName` says otherwise |
| `UuidV7` | `uuid` | Prism, before the `INSERT`: time-ordered UUIDs that index well |

Without `#[Prism\GeneratedValue]`, your code assigns the identifier before `persist()`.

sections.title: Mapping entities › Columns and types
sections.content:
Every property with `#[Prism\Column]` is stored. A property without a mapping attribute is never read nor written by Prism.

Prism deduces the type and the nullability from the PHP type:

| PHP type | Column type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `string` | `VARCHAR(255)` unless `length` says otherwise |
| `int` | `integer` | |
| `bool` | `boolean` | |
| `float` | `float` | |
| `\DateTimeImmutable` | `datetime_immutable` | |
| `array` | `json` | |
| a backed enum | `string` or `integer` | the type of the enum's values |
| `?string`, `?int`… | nullable | |

Set `type` for the other types: `text`, `bigint`, `smallint`, `decimal`, `date_immutable`, `time_immutable`, `uuid` and `binary`.

```php
enum WarehouseKind: string
{
    case Own = 'own';
    case Partner = 'partner';
}

#[Prism\Entity]
final class Depot
{
    #[Prism\Id, Prism\GeneratedValue]
    public ?int $id = null;

    #[Prism\Column(length: 20, unique: true)]
    public string $code;

    #[Prism\Column(type: 'text')]
    public ?string $notes = null;

    #[Prism\Column]
    public WarehouseKind $kind = WarehouseKind::Own;

    #[Prism\Column(type: 'decimal', precision: 12, scale: 2)]
    public string $insuredValue = '0.00';

    #[Prism\Column(type: 'date_immutable')]
    public ?\DateTimeImmutable $openedOn = null;

    #[Prism\Column]
    public array $openingHours = [];
}
```

The rules that keep data exact:

- A `decimal` is always a PHP `string`: an amount is never rounded by a `float`. `precision` and `scale` are required.
- Dates are `\DateTimeImmutable`. A `\DateTime` property is refused when the mapping is validated.
- The nullability comes from the PHP type. `#[Prism\Column(nullable: false)]` on a `?string` is a contradiction, and an error.

The other options of `#[Prism\Column]`:

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The column name, instead of the property name in snake case |
| `length` | The length of a `string` or `binary` column |
| `fixed` | A fixed-length column: `CHAR` or `BINARY` instead of `VARCHAR` or `VARBINARY` |
| `unique` | A unique constraint on this column alone |
| `default` | The default value of the column in the database |
| `enumType` | The backed enum of the property, when it cannot be read from the PHP type |
| `insertable`, `updatable` | `false` leaves the column out of `INSERT` or `UPDATE` statements: for columns computed by the database |
| `sensitive` | The value is masked in the [audit log](/guide/audit) |

Custom types extend `Prism\Dbal\Type\Type` and are registered in the `TypeRegistry` of the connection; in Symfony, a service tagged `prism.type` is registered for you.

sections.title: Migrations
sections.content:
A migration is a versioned PHP class that changes the schema. Prism generates it from the difference between your entities and the database, checks it before it runs, and refuses to run a migration that changed after it was applied.

The commands below are the Symfony ones (`bin/console`); without Symfony, they are the same with `vendor/bin/prism`. Every option is listed in the [command reference](/bundle/commands).

sections.title: Migrations › The workflow
sections.content:
1. Change your entities.
2. Generate the migration: `bin/console db:migrations:diff`.
3. Read it. Fix it if needed.
4. Lint it against the database: `bin/console db:migrations:lint`.
5. Run it: `bin/console db:migrations:migrate`.

`diff` writes nothing when the database already matches the entities.

sections.title: Migrations › A migration
Migrations › Renames
Migrations › Going back
sections.content:
`diff` writes a `down()` only when it is safe. When the migration destroys data, a dropped column for example, its `down()` throws `IrreversibleMigrationException`: there is no way to bring the data back.

```console
$ bin/console db:migrations:migrate Version20261020120000   # back to that version
$ bin/console db:migrations:migrate 0                       # revert everything
$ bin/console db:migrations:execute Version20261027093000 --down
```

sections.title: Migrations › Running migrations
sections.content:
```console
$ bin/console db:migrations:status
$ bin/console db:migrations:migrate --dry-run
$ bin/console db:migrations:migrate
```

- **Transactions.** Under PostgreSQL, each migration runs in a transaction and a failure leaves nothing behind. MySQL and MariaDB commit each DDL statement implicitly: a migration that fails halfway stays half applied. The command says which migrations run without a transaction before it starts.
- **Checksums.** Prism stores a checksum of each applied migration in `prism_migration_versions`. A migration modified after it ran blocks `migrate`, until you restore it or pass `--allow-modified`.
- **Production.** In the `prod` environment, `migrate` asks for confirmation, unless `--no-interaction`.

sections.content: In development, `db:schema:update` brings the database in line with the entities without a migration: `--dump-sql` shows the SQL, `--force` runs it. It never drops a table that is not mapped unless you add `--complete`.

sections.title: Multi-tenancy
sections.content:
A B2B application often serves many customer companies, the *tenants*, from one database. Every query must then be limited to the current tenant, and forgetting it once leaks one customer's data to another. Prism makes this filter automatic and impossible to forget: it fails closed.

The examples run on the demo application, whose tenants are two companies, Acme and Globex. Acme is the current tenant.

sections.title: Multi-tenancy › Tenanted entities
Multi-tenancy › What Prism does
Multi-tenancy › No tenant, no query
Multi-tenancy › Setting the tenant
Multi-tenancy › Shared rows
Multi-tenancy › Raw SQL
Multi-tenancy › Entity filters
Multi-tenancy › In Symfony
sections.content:
```yaml
# config/packages/prism.yaml
prism:
    tenancy:
        type: integer           # integer, bigint or uuid
        resolver:
            subdomain: example.com
        loader: App\Tenancy\CompanyLoader
        # guard: log            # default: exception in debug, log otherwise
```

The bundle sets the tenant of each request from **one** source:

| `resolver` | Source | Runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `header: X-Tenant-Id` | A request header; **only behind a gateway that sets it itself** | Before the firewall |
| `subdomain: example.com` | `acme` in `acme.example.com` | Before the firewall |
| `user: true` | The logged-in user, a `TenantAwareUserInterface` | After the firewall |

A subdomain is a name, not an identifier: a `TenantLoader` service translates it, like the demo's `CompanyLoader`. With the `user` strategy, the user entity must not be tenanted, since the firewall loads it before the tenant is known. Without a `resolver`, set the tenant yourself, through the `StackTenantContext` service.

Between two requests of a worker, the context is reset. The `db:*` commands run in system mode: they administer the whole database. In development, the **Tenant** panel of the profiler shows the tenant of the request, how it was resolved, and the `runAs()` and `runAsSystem()` calls.

In a test, set the tenant before using the entities:

```php no-run
static::getContainer()->get(StackTenantContext::class)->setTenantId(1);
```

Avoiding N+1 queries
sections.content:
An N+1 is one query to load a list, then one more query per element to load a relation: 100 orders, then 100 queries for their customers. It is the most common performance problem of ORMs, and it hides in innocent loops and templates.

Prism prevents it by default, and reports the cases it cannot prevent.

sections.title: Avoiding N+1 queries › Batch fetching
Avoiding N+1 queries › Batch size
sections.content:
A batch holds 100 identifiers at most; a larger cohort is loaded in several `IN` queries. Change the size per relation, or globally:

```php no-run
#[Prism\ManyToOne(batchSize: 250)]
public Customer $customer;
```

```yaml
# config/packages/prism.yaml
prism:
    entity_managers:
        default:
            batch_size: 250
```

Without Symfony, the global size is the `batchSize` argument of the `EntityManager` constructor.

sections.title: Avoiding N+1 queries › Turning it off
sections.content:
Batch fetching loads relations that a loop may not use: an order list that shows the customer of the first order only would load all of them. Turn it off for one relation, or for the entities of one query:

```php no-run
#[Prism\ManyToOne(batch: false)]
public Customer $customer;
```

```php
$o = Order_::as('o');

$orders = $em->query($o)
    ->where($o->status->eq('open'))
    ->withoutBatchFetch()
    ->getResult();
```

PHPStan
sections.content: Prism's PHPStan extension checks at analysis time what Prism would otherwise check at run time: the fields of your repository calls, the DTOs of your projections, the type of your repositories and the properties that Prism writes for you.

sections.title: PHPStan › Install
sections.content:
```bash
composer require --dev prism-orm/phpstan phpstan/extension-installer
```

`phpstan/extension-installer` loads the extension. The extension reads your mapping and the generated metamodel; tell it where the metamodel is when it is not in `var/cache/prism/metamodel`:

```neon
# phpstan.neon
parameters:
    prism:
        metamodelDir: %currentWorkingDirectory%/var/cache/dev/prism/metamodel/default
```

In Symfony, the metamodel of each entity manager is in `var/cache/<env>/prism/metamodel/<entity manager>`, generated when the cache warms up: run `bin/console cache:warmup` before PHPStan in your CI.

sections.title: PHPStan › What it reports
sections.content:
Given this code, with the demo's `Customer` entity and a `CustomerRevenue` DTO whose constructor takes `string $customer, int $invoices, string $total, ?\DateTimeImmutable $lastInvoice`:

```php no-run
$this->em->getRepository(Customer::class)->findBy(['emial' => 'a@b.c']);
$this->em->getRepository(Customer::class)->findBy(['orders' => 3]);

$i = Invoice_::as('i');
$this->em->query($i)
    ->selectInto(CustomerRevenue::class, customer: $i->number, invoices: $i->total->sum(), total: $i->total->sum())
    ->getResult();
```

PHPStan reports:

```console
$ vendor/bin/phpstan analyse
 ------ ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Line   Report.php
 ------ ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  19     Unknown field App\Entity\Customer::$emial in the criteria of
         findBy(). Did you mean "email"?
         🪪  prism.findBy.unknownField
  20     App\Entity\Customer::$orders is a collection: findBy() compares only
         fields and owning ToOne relations; join it with the typed query
         builder instead.
         🪪  prism.findBy.relation
  23     The parameter $lastInvoice of
         App\Report\CustomerRevenue::__construct() is required but not
         selected: select it as lastInvoice: ...
         🪪  prism.selectInto.missingParameter
  24     The selection "invoices" is string|null, but $invoices of
         App\Report\CustomerRevenue::__construct() accepts int.
         🪪  prism.selectInto.typeMismatch
  24     The selection "total" is string|null, but $total of
         App\Report\CustomerRevenue::__construct() accepts string.
         🪪  prism.selectInto.typeMismatch
 ------ ----------------------------------------------------------------------

 [ERROR] Found 5 errors
```

The last error is about `NULL`: `SUM()` of an empty set is `NULL`, so a sum is typed `string|null`, and the parameter that receives it must be `?string`.

| Check | Errors |
| --- | --- |
| The criteria and order keys of `findBy()`, `findOneBy()`, `count()` and `iterate()` are fields of the entity, with a suggestion for a typo | `prism.findBy.unknownField` |
| A criterion is a field or an owning `ManyToOne` / `OneToOne`, not a collection | `prism.findBy.relation` |
| An order value is a `Prism\Dbal\Query\Order` case | `prism.findBy.invalidOrder` |
| Every selection of `selectInto()` is named after a constructor parameter | `prism.selectInto.unnamed`, `prism.selectInto.unknownParameter` |
| Every required parameter is selected | `prism.selectInto.missingParameter` |
| Every selection has a type that its parameter accepts | `prism.selectInto.typeMismatch` |

The typed query builder needs no rule of its own: its fields are typed PHP methods, so `$o->status->eq(42)` or `$i->total->gt(100)` are plain type errors for PHPStan.

sections.title: PHPStan › Types it infers
sections.content:
- `$em->getRepository(Invoice::class)` returns the `repositoryClass` of the entity, `InvoiceRepository`, so its own methods are known without a `@var`. Without a declared repository, it is `EntityRepository<Invoice>`, whose `find()` returns `?Invoice` and `findBy()` returns `list<Invoice>`.
- `$em->query($o)->getResult()` returns `list<Order>`, `getOneOrNull()` returns `?Order`, and `selectInto(Dto::class, ...)->getResult()` returns `list<Dto>`.
- The mapped properties of an entity are written by Prism when it loads the entity, without the constructor. PHPStan does not report them as uninitialized, never written or never read. Properties that are not mapped are still checked.

sections.title: Typed queries
sections.content:
The typed query builder writes queries without a single field-name string. For each entity, Prism generates a metamodel class, `Order_` for `Order`, whose properties are typed fields; a query is built from them and returns typed results.

```php
$o = Order_::as('o');

$orders = $em->query($o)
    ->where($o->status->eq('open'))
    ->andWhere($o->placedAt->gte(new \DateTimeImmutable('2026-03-01')))
    ->orderBy($o->placedAt->desc())
    ->limit(10)
    ->getResult(); // list<Order>
```

`Order_::as('o')` names the entity in the query; `$em->query($o)` starts a query whose results are `Order` entities.

sections.title: Typed queries › The metamodel
sections.content:
The metamodel classes are generated from your entities, and never written by hand:

- **In Symfony**, they are generated in `var/cache/<env>/prism/metamodel` when the cache warms up, and regenerated in development when an entity changes.
- **Without Symfony**, run `vendor/bin/prism db:metamodel:generate` after changing an entity, and register the autoloader once, in `prism.php` for example:

```php no-run
use Prism\Orm\Query\Metamodel\MetamodelAutoloader;

MetamodelAutoloader::register(__DIR__ . '/var/cache/prism/metamodel');
```

The generated files are not versioned. For your IDE, the command also writes a stub (`.prism/metamodel.php`) and PhpStorm metadata, so `Order_` and its fields autocomplete.

Each field has the methods that make sense for its type, and only accepts values of that type:

| Field | Comparisons |
| --- | --- |
| string | `eq`, `neq`, `lt`, `lte`, `gt`, `gte`, `in`, `notIn`, `between`, `like` |
| int, float, decimal | `eq`, `neq`, `lt`, `lte`, `gt`, `gte`, `in`, `notIn`, `between` |
| date and time | the same, with `\DateTimeImmutable` values |
| bool | `eq`, `neq` |
| enum | `eq`, `neq`, `in`, `notIn`, with cases of the enum |
| relation | `eq`, `in` (entities or identifiers), `isNull`, `isNotNull` |

Every field also has `isNull()`, `isNotNull()`, `asc()` and `desc()`. A decimal compares with a string (`$i->total->gt('100.00')`), never a float. Passing a value of the wrong type is a PHP type error, and PHPStan reports it before the code runs.

Typed queries › Joins
Typed queries › Aggregates and projections
Typed queries › JSON fields
sections.content:
A path inside a `json` column is read with `path()`, then typed explicitly:

```php no-run
$p = Product_::as('p');

$red = $em->query($p)
    ->where($p->attributes->path('color')->asString()->eq('red'))
    ->andWhere($p->attributes->path('sizes', 0)->asInt()->gte(38))
    ->getResult();
```

`asString()`, `asInt()` and `asDecimal()` give an expression with the comparisons of that type. A missing key or a JSON `null` is `NULL` on all four databases.

sections.title: Typed queries › Pagination
Typed queries › Results
sections.content:
| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `getResult()` | `list<T>` |
| `getOneOrNull()` | `?T`; throws `NonUniqueResultException` if there are several |
| `paginate($page, $perPage)` | `Paginator<T>` |
| `selectInto(Dto::class, ...)->getResult()` | `list<Dto>` |

Soft-deleted entities are left out; `withDeleted()` includes them. When a query needs SQL that the builder does not cover, `toSql()` and `getParameters()` show what it generates, and `getConnection()` gives the DBAL connection to run your own. Raw SQL on a tenanted table still has to filter on the tenant: see [multi-tenancy](/guide/multi-tenancy#raw-sql).

sections.title: Relations
sections.content: Prism supports the four kinds of relations: `ManyToOne`, `OneToMany`, `OneToOne` and `ManyToMany`. A relation is a property typed with the target entity, or with `Collection` for the "many" side.

sections.title: Relations › Many to one
Relations › One to many
Relations › One to many › The owning side
Relations › One to many › Sorting and indexing
sections.content:
```php no-run
/** @var Collection<string, Product> */
#[Prism\ManyToMany(targetEntity: Product::class, indexBy: 'sku')]
#[Prism\OrderBy(['name' => Order::Asc])]
public Collection $products;
```

`#[Prism\OrderBy]` sorts a `OneToMany` or `ManyToMany` collection in SQL when it loads, with `Prism\Dbal\Query\Order`, the sort order of `findBy()` and of the query builder, and the order is kept when the collection is loaded in a batch. `indexBy` keys the collection by a field of the target: `$priceList->products['SKU-042']`.

sections.title: Relations › One to one
Relations › Many to many
Relations › Cascades and orphans
sections.content:
A new entity reachable from a managed one must be persisted. If it is not, the flush throws `UnpersistedRelationException`, which names the entity, the field and the path. To persist it with its parent:

```php no-run
/** @var Collection<int, OrderLine> */
#[Prism\OneToMany(targetEntity: OrderLine::class, mappedBy: 'order', cascade: [Prism\Cascade::Persist], orphanRemoval: true)]
public Collection $lines;
```

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `cascade: [Prism\Cascade::Persist]` | `persist()` on the parent persists the new entities it reaches |
| `cascade: [Prism\Cascade::Remove]` | `remove()` on the parent removes the related entities, with their events |
| `cascade: [Prism\Cascade::Detach]` | `detach()` on the parent detaches them |
| `orphanRemoval: true` | An entity removed from the collection is deleted at the flush |

`cascade: Remove` is applied by Prism, entity by entity, with lifecycle events; `onDelete: Cascade` is applied by the database, without them. The mapping validator warns when both are set on the same relation. An orphan cannot be attached to another parent in the same flush.

sections.title: Relations › Lazy loading
sections.content:
A relation is loaded when you first use it, never before:

- a `ManyToOne` or owning `OneToOne` is a reference: an object of the target class whose identifier is readable without a query;
- a collection loads its elements on first access.

```php
$order = $em->getRepository(Order::class)->findOneBy(['reference' => 'ORD-00003']);

echo $order->customer->id;   // no query: the identifier is known
echo $order->customer->name; // loads the customer
```

There is no proxy class: references are PHP 8.4 lazy ghosts, so a `final` entity works. The `fetch` option changes when a relation loads:

| `fetch` | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `Fetch::Lazy` (default) | On first access |
| `Fetch::Eager` | Right after the query that loads the owner, in one query for all of them |
| `Fetch::ExtraLazy` | For collections: `count()` runs a `SELECT COUNT(*)` without loading the elements |

When a relation is loaded for one entity, Prism loads it for every entity of the same query at once, in batches of 100. This is what keeps loops free of N+1 queries; `batchSize` changes the batch size of a relation, and `batch: false` turns batching off for it.

sections.title: Vector search
sections.content:
Store embeddings next to your business data, index them, and search them from the repository: by meaning with `nearest()`, or by meaning and words together with `hybridSearch()`. No SQL specific to the database, and the usual filters (tenant, soft delete, criteria) apply before the ranking.

| Database | Vector type | Index | Full text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MariaDB 11.8+ | `VECTOR(n)` | HNSW (`VECTOR INDEX`) | `FULLTEXT` |
| PostgreSQL 15+ with pgvector 0.8+ | `vector(n)` | HNSW | GIN index on `to_tsvector()` |
| SQLite | text, distances computed in PHP | none: for tests and development | scored in PHP |
| MySQL | refused: Community has neither a vector distance nor a vector index | | |

Prism creates the `vector` extension of PostgreSQL with the schema, and refuses a pgvector older than 0.8.

The examples of this page are not run by the documentation tests, which also run on MySQL: the [demo application](https://github.com/IMAMx39/prism/tree/main/demo) and Prism's functional tests run the same code on MariaDB, PostgreSQL and SQLite.

sections.title: Vector search › A vector field
Vector search › Indexes
sections.content:
`#[VectorIndex]` builds an HNSW index on the field: `distance` is `Distance::Cosine` (default), `Distance::Euclidean` or `Distance::InnerProduct`; `m` (default 16) and `efConstruction` (default 64) tune the graph. The platform you target refuses what it cannot do, when the mapping is validated rather than at the first query:

- MariaDB indexes only `NOT NULL` vector columns, one vector index per table, and has no inner product.
- pgvector indexes up to 2,000 dimensions with HNSW.

On MariaDB, give the graph room: `mhnsw_max_cache_size` (16 MB by default) should hold the whole index, about 2 KB per vector of 768 dimensions. See [Measures](#measures).

`#[FullTextIndex]` is the index `hybridSearch()` searches, with the stemming of its `language` on PostgreSQL (`english`, `french`, `simple`…). Migrations create both: `createVectorIndex()` and `createFullTextIndex()` in a migration, generated by `db:migrations:diff`.

sections.title: Vector search › nearest()
Vector search › hybridSearch()
Vector search › Keeping embeddings up to date
Vector search › Measures
sections.content:
The demo searches the Prism documentation: 324 sections, `nomic-embed-text:v1.5` vectors (768 dimensions) on PostgreSQL, and 60 questions annotated by hand with the sections that answer them (112 in all). `bin/console app:docs:evaluate` ranks the sections for each question:

| Search | Recall@10 | MRR@10 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hybridSearch()` | **0.922** | 0.777 |
| vector only | 0.903 | **0.807** |
| full text only | 0.711 | 0.529 |

The hybrid search finds more of the relevant sections in its first ten results; the vector search alone more often puts the best one first. The corpus is small: these figures compare the three rankings with each other, they are not a public benchmark.

`make bench-vector` loads 100,000 random vectors of 768 dimensions into MariaDB and PostgreSQL, then times `nearest(limit: 10)`, entities hydrated:

| Database | `nearest()` p50 | p95 | Filtered to 1 % of the rows, p95 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MariaDB 11.8.6 | 21 ms | **22 ms** | 410 ms |
| PostgreSQL 16, pgvector 0.8.7 | 27 ms | **31 ms** | 29 ms |

Measured on 2026-10-28: Intel Xeon Gold 5218, 8 cores, 7.7 GB of RAM shared with the other services, the databases in Docker; HNSW with `m = 16`, cosine distance; 200 searches to warm up, 200 measured, each with a new vector. The script is `tools/bench/vector-nearest.php`.

- **Size the HNSW cache of MariaDB.** MariaDB keeps the graph in `mhnsw_max_cache_size`, 16 MB by default: far too little for 100,000 vectors of 768 dimensions, whose graph is then read again on each search. The benchmark sets it to 1 GB; with the default, the same search takes 65 ms at p95 and the index takes 23 minutes to build instead of 3.
- **A selective filter costs more on MariaDB.** When a filter keeps few rows, the HNSW index of MariaDB returns too few of them, and Prism falls back to an exact search over the rows the filter keeps, through the index of the filtered column. Its cost grows with those rows and with the InnoDB buffer pool (128 MB here). PostgreSQL scans its index iteratively until it has enough rows. Index the column you filter on, as Prism does for `tenant_id`. The migration linter warns (L21) when a vector index is created on a tenanted table of MariaDB where one tenant, among others, has more than 10,000 rows.
