Attributes
sections.content:
Every attribute of Prism, with each of its parameters. The mapping attributes live in `Prism\Orm\Mapping` and are written with the `Prism\` alias (`use Prism\Orm\Mapping as Prism;`); the others are named with their namespace.

This page is checked against the code: a parameter added to an attribute fails the build until it is documented here.

sections.title: Attributes › Entities › `#[Entity]`
sections.content:
Makes a class an entity. Class attribute. See [Mapping entities](/guide/mapping#entities-and-tables).

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `repositoryClass` | `null` | The class returned by `getRepository()`; it extends `EntityRepository`. `null`: `EntityRepository` |
| `trackingPolicy` | `TrackingPolicy::Implicit` | `Implicit`: every managed entity is compared at flush. `Explicit`: only the entities passed to `persist()` since the last flush |
| `readOnly` | `false` | The entity is never compared at flush: it is inserted and deleted, never updated |

sections.title: Attributes › Entities › `#[Table]`
sections.content:
The table of the entity. Class attribute.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `null` | The table name. `null`: the class name in snake case (`OrderLine` → `order_line`) |
| `options` | `[]` | MySQL and MariaDB table options: `engine`, `charset`, `collation`, `comment`. Any other key is refused |

sections.title: Attributes › Identifiers › `#[Id]`
sections.content: Marks the identifier property. Each entity has exactly one. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Identifiers › `#[GeneratedValue]`
sections.content:
Lets the identifier be generated. Property attribute, next to `#[Id]`.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `strategy` | `GenerationStrategy::Auto` | `Auto`: `Identity` under MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite, `Sequence` under PostgreSQL. `Identity`: auto-increment column. `Sequence`: database sequence. `UuidV7`: generated by Prism before the `INSERT`, on a `uuid` column |
| `sequenceName` | `null` | The sequence of `Auto` or `Sequence`. `null`: `<table>_id_seq` |

sections.title: Attributes › Fields › `#[Column]`
sections.content:
Stores a property in a column. Every `null` parameter is deduced from the PHP type. See [Columns and types](/guide/mapping#columns-and-types).

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `null` | The column name. `null`: the property name in snake case |
| `type` | `null` | `string`, `text`, `integer`, `bigint`, `smallint`, `boolean`, `decimal`, `float`, `datetime_immutable`, `date_immutable`, `time_immutable`, `json`, `uuid`, `binary`, or a custom type. `null`: deduced from the PHP type |
| `length` | `null` | Length of a `string` or `binary` column. `null`: 255 for a `string` |
| `nullable` | `null` | `null`: deduced from the PHP type (`?string`). A value that contradicts the type is a mapping error |
| `unique` | `false` | A unique constraint on this column alone; per tenant on a `#[Tenanted]` entity, on live rows on a `#[SoftDeletable]` one |
| `precision` | `null` | Total number of digits of a `decimal`, from 1 to 65; required for a `decimal` |
| `scale` | `null` | Digits after the decimal point of a `decimal`, from 0 to 30, at most `precision`; required for a `decimal` |
| `enumType` | `null` | The backed enum of the property. `null`: read from the PHP type |
| `default` | `null` | The default value of the column in the database |
| `sensitive` | `false` | The value is written as `***` in the audit log |
| `insertable` | `true` | `false`: the column is left out of `INSERT` statements |
| `updatable` | `true` | `false`: the column is left out of `UPDATE` statements, for a column computed by the database |
| `fixed` | `false` | Fixed length: `CHAR` or `BINARY` instead of `VARCHAR` or `VARBINARY`; needs a `length` |
| `dimensions` | `null` | The dimension of a `vector` column, from 1 to 16,000; required for a `vector`. A vector of another size is refused before it is written. See [Vector search](/guide/vector-search#a-vector-field) |
| `lazy` | `null` | `true`: the field is not read with the entity, only on first access, for the whole batch. `null`: `true` for a `Prism\Orm\Vector\Vector` property, `false` otherwise; only a `Vector` can be lazy |

sections.title: Attributes › Fields › `#[Version]`
sections.content: Optimistic locking: the field is checked and incremented by each `UPDATE`, and a concurrent change throws `OptimisticLockException`. On an `int` or `\DateTimeImmutable` property, next to `#[Column]`. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Embeddables › `#[Embeddable]`
sections.content: Makes a class a value object stored in the columns of the entity that contains it. Class attribute; its properties carry `#[Column]`. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Embeddables › `#[Embedded]`
sections.content:
Stores an embeddable in the entity. Property attribute. A nullable embeddable is `null` when all its columns are `NULL`.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `class` | `null` | The embeddable class. `null`: the property type |
| `columnPrefix` | `null` | `null`: the property name in snake case and `_` (`billing_address_`). `false`: no prefix. A string: that prefix |

sections.title: Attributes › Indexes › `#[Index]`
sections.content:
An index on one or more fields. Class attribute, repeatable. On a `#[Tenanted]` entity, `tenant_id` comes first.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | | The fields indexed, in order: PHP properties, owning `ManyToOne` or `OneToOne` relations (their foreign key column), or `address.city` for a field of an embeddable |
| `name` | `null` | The index name. `null`: generated from a hash of the columns, stable from one diff to the next |
| `where` | `null` | Accepted, but not applied yet: the index covers every row, which makes it wider, never wrong. Partial indexes with a free condition are planned after 1.0 |

sections.title: Attributes › Indexes › `#[UniqueConstraint]`
sections.content:
A unique constraint on one or more fields. Class attribute, repeatable. On a `#[Tenanted]` entity, unique per tenant; on a `#[SoftDeletable]` entity, unique among the rows that are not deleted.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | | The fields of the constraint: PHP properties or owning `ManyToOne` / `OneToOne` relations |
| `name` | `null` | The constraint name. `null`: generated, stable |
| `where` | `null` | Not supported yet: a unique constraint with a `where` is refused when the schema is built, since enforcing it without its condition would reject valid rows |

sections.title: Attributes › Vector search
sections.content: See [Vector search](/guide/vector-search). Not on MySQL, which has no vector type: these attributes are refused when the mapping is validated for it.

sections.title: Attributes › Vector search › `#[VectorIndex]`
sections.content:
An HNSW index on a `vector` field, used by `nearest()`, `hybridSearch()` and `distanceTo()`. Property attribute, next to `#[Column(dimensions: …)]`. On MariaDB, the column must be `NOT NULL`, and a table has one vector index at most.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `distance` | `Distance::Cosine` | `Distance::Cosine`, `Distance::Euclidean`, or `Distance::InnerProduct` (PostgreSQL and SQLite only). Also the distance of `nearest()` on this field |
| `m` | `16` | Connections per node of the graph, from 2 to 100 |
| `efConstruction` | `64` | Search width while building the graph, from 4 to 1,000, at least `2 × m` |

sections.title: Attributes › Vector search › `#[FullTextIndex]`
sections.content:
A full-text index on text fields, searched by `hybridSearch()`. Class attribute, repeatable. `FULLTEXT` on MySQL and MariaDB, a GIN index on `to_tsvector()` on PostgreSQL, scored in PHP on SQLite.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | | The `string` or `text` fields indexed |
| `language` | `'simple'` | The text search configuration of PostgreSQL: `english`, `french`, `simple` (no stemming)… Ignored by the other databases |
| `name` | `null` | The index name, and `HybridOptions::$fullTextIndex` when the entity has several. `null`: generated, stable |

sections.title: Attributes › Vector search › `#[EmbeddedVector]`
sections.content:
Keeps a `vector` field computed from text fields. Property attribute, next to `#[Column(dimensions: …)]`. Adds two columns without properties, `<column>_stale` and `<column>_model`. A change of a source field makes the vector stale at flush; after the commit, the stale rows go to the embedding scheduler. A stale vector is left out of `nearest()`. See [Keeping embeddings up to date](/guide/vector-search#keeping-embeddings-up-to-date).

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | | The `string` or `text` field, or the list of fields, whose text is embedded, joined by a blank line |
| `model` | `'default'` | The name of the embedding provider, in the `EmbeddingProviderRegistry` (`prism.embeddings.providers` in Symfony); its dimension must be the one of the column |

sections.title: Attributes › Relations
sections.content: See [Relations](/guide/relations). In the tables below, `cascade` is a list of `Cascade::Persist`, `Cascade::Remove` and `Cascade::Detach`, and `fetch` is `Fetch::Lazy`, `Fetch::Eager` or `Fetch::ExtraLazy`.

sections.title: Attributes › Relations › `#[ManyToOne]`
sections.content:
The owning side of a many-to-one relation: it holds the foreign key.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `targetEntity` | `null` | The target class. `null`: the property type |
| `inversedBy` | `null` | The property of the target that holds the other side |
| `cascade` | `[]` | Operations propagated to the target |
| `fetch` | `Fetch::Lazy` | When the target loads |
| `joinColumn` | `null` | The foreign key column. `null`: `<property>_id` |
| `onDelete` | `OnDelete::Restrict` | What the database does when the target row is deleted: `Restrict`, `Cascade`, `SetNull`, `NoAction` |
| `batchSize` | `null` | Batch size of batch fetching, from 1 to 1000. `null`: the entity manager's, 100 by default |
| `batch` | `true` | `false`: no batch fetching for this relation |
| `foreignKey` | `null` | The foreign key constraint name. `null`: generated, stable |

sections.title: Attributes › Relations › `#[OneToMany]`
sections.content:
The inverse side of a `ManyToOne`, as a `Collection`. It has no column.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `targetEntity` | | The class of the elements; required |
| `mappedBy` | | The `ManyToOne` property of the target; required |
| `cascade` | `[]` | Operations propagated to the elements |
| `fetch` | `Fetch::Lazy` | `ExtraLazy`: `count()` runs a `COUNT` query without loading the elements |
| `orphanRemoval` | `false` | An element removed from the collection is deleted at the flush |
| `indexBy` | `null` | A field of the target whose values key the collection |
| `batchSize` | `null` | Batch size of batch fetching, from 1 to 1000 |
| `batch` | `true` | `false`: no batch fetching for this collection |

sections.title: Attributes › Relations › `#[OneToOne]`
sections.content:
A one-to-one relation. The owning side holds a unique foreign key; the inverse side has `mappedBy` and no column.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `targetEntity` | `null` | The target class. `null`: the property type |
| `mappedBy` | `null` | On the inverse side: the property of the target that owns the relation |
| `inversedBy` | `null` | On the owning side: the property of the target that holds the other side |
| `cascade` | `[]` | Operations propagated to the target |
| `fetch` | `Fetch::Lazy` | When the target loads; the inverse side is always loaded with its owner, in a batch |
| `joinColumn` | `null` | Owning side only: the foreign key column. `null`: `<property>_id` |
| `onDelete` | `OnDelete::Restrict` | Owning side only: what the database does when the target row is deleted |
| `orphanRemoval` | `false` | A target replaced or set to `null` is deleted at the flush |
| `batchSize` | `null` | Batch size of batch fetching, from 1 to 1000 |
| `batch` | `true` | `false`: no batch fetching for this relation |
| `foreignKey` | `null` | Owning side only: the foreign key constraint name |

sections.title: Attributes › Relations › `#[ManyToMany]`
sections.content:
A many-to-many relation through a join table. The owning side, with `inversedBy` or without another side, writes the join table.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `targetEntity` | | The class of the elements; required |
| `mappedBy` | `null` | On the inverse side: the property of the target that owns the relation |
| `inversedBy` | `null` | On the owning side: the property of the target that holds the other side |
| `cascade` | `[]` | Operations propagated to the elements |
| `fetch` | `Fetch::Lazy` | `ExtraLazy`: `count()` without loading the elements |
| `indexBy` | `null` | A field of the target whose values key the collection |
| `batchSize` | `null` | Batch size of batch fetching, from 1 to 1000 |
| `batch` | `true` | `false`: no batch fetching for this collection |

sections.title: Attributes › Relations › `#[JoinTable]`
sections.content:
The join table of a `ManyToMany`, on the owning side.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `null` | The table name. `null`: `<owner table>_<target table>` |
| `joinColumn` | `null` | The column pointing to the owner. `null`: `<owner table>_id` |
| `inverseJoinColumn` | `null` | The column pointing to the target. `null`: `<target table>_id` |
| `onDelete` | `OnDelete::Cascade` | What the database does with the links when an owner or a target is deleted |

sections.title: Attributes › Relations › `#[OrderBy]`
sections.content:
The order of a `OneToMany` or `ManyToMany` collection, applied in SQL and kept by batch fetching.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | | Field → `Order::Asc` or `Order::Desc`, of `Prism\Dbal\Query\Order`, the enum `findBy()` and the query builder take too: `['position' => Order::Asc]` |

sections.title: Attributes › Lifecycle › `#[HasLifecycleCallbacks]`
sections.content: Enables the lifecycle callbacks declared on the methods of the entity. Class attribute. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Lifecycle › `#[PrePersist]`
sections.content: The method runs before the `INSERT` of the entity, in the transaction of the flush; a change it makes is inserted. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Lifecycle › `#[PostPersist]`
sections.content: The method runs after the commit of the flush that inserted the entity. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Lifecycle › `#[PreUpdate]`
sections.content: The method runs before the `UPDATE` of the entity; a change it makes is included. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Lifecycle › `#[PostUpdate]`
sections.content: The method runs after the commit of the flush that updated the entity. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Lifecycle › `#[PreRemove]`
sections.content: The method runs when `remove()` is called, before the entity is scheduled for deletion. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Lifecycle › `#[PostRemove]`
sections.content: The method runs after the commit of the flush that deleted the entity. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Lifecycle › `#[PostLoad]`
sections.content: The method runs after the entity is loaded from the database, never when the identity map returns an entity already loaded. Since the constructor is not called, this is where derived state is computed. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Lifecycle › `#[EntityListeners]`
sections.content:
Classes whose methods, carrying the lifecycle attributes above, receive the entity as first argument. Class attribute.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `listeners` | | The listener classes. In Symfony, a class with `#[AsEntityListener]` is a service |

sections.title: Attributes › Multi-tenancy and behaviors › `#[Tenanted]`
sections.content:
Isolates the entity by tenant: a `tenant_id` column, filled and filtered by Prism. See [Multi-tenancy](/guide/multi-tenancy).

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `global` | `false` | Rows without a tenant are shared: every tenant reads them, only the system mode writes them |
| `column` | `null` | The name of the tenant column. `null`: `tenant_id` |
| `strictForeignKeys` | `false` | Composite foreign keys `(tenant_id, id)`, so that the database itself refuses a cross-tenant relation. Not supported in 1.0, which has single-column keys: `true` is refused by the mapping validator. Prism refuses cross-tenant relations at flush instead |

sections.title: Attributes › Multi-tenancy and behaviors › `#[Timestampable]`
sections.content:
Sets the creation and update dates, in UTC. See [Audit and behaviors](/guide/audit#timestamps-and-authors).

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createdAt` | `'createdAt'` | The mapped field set at `INSERT`, unless already set |
| `updatedAt` | `'updatedAt'` | The mapped field set when another field changes. `null`: never set |

sections.title: Attributes › Multi-tenancy and behaviors › `#[Blameable]`
sections.content:
Sets the author of the creation and of the last update, from the `ActorProvider`.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createdBy` | `'createdBy'` | The mapped field set at `INSERT`, unless already set |
| `updatedBy` | `'updatedBy'` | The mapped field set when another field changes. `null`: never set |

sections.title: Attributes › Multi-tenancy and behaviors › `#[SoftDeletable]`
sections.content:
Turns `remove()` into an `UPDATE` of the deletion date; deleted rows are left out of reads. See [Soft delete](/guide/audit#soft-delete).

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `'deletedAt'` | The mapped, nullable `\DateTimeImmutable` field that holds the deletion date |

sections.title: Attributes › Multi-tenancy and behaviors › `#[Auditable]`
sections.content:
Writes each change of the entity into `prism_audit_log`, in the transaction of the flush. See [Audit log](/guide/audit#audit-log).

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exclude` | `[]` | Fields left out of the changeset, `updatedAt` for example |
| `retention` | `null` | How long the rows are kept, as an ISO 8601 duration (`'P10Y'`), for `db:audit:purge`. `null`: purged only with `--older-than` |

sections.title: Attributes › Symfony bundle › `#[UniqueEntity]`
sections.content:
`Prism\Bundle\Validator\UniqueEntity`: a validation constraint, true when no other entity of the class has the same values. Class attribute, repeatable.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | | A field or a `ToOne` relation, or a list of them checked together |
| `message` | `'This value is already used.'` | The violation message |
| `errorPath` | `null` | The property the violation is attached to. `null`: the first field |
| `ignoreNull` | `true` | A `null` value is never a duplicate, like in a database unique constraint |
| `entityManager` | `null` | The entity manager to query. `null`: the one that maps the class |
| `groups` | `null` | Validation groups |
| `payload` | `null` | Symfony's constraint payload |

sections.title: Attributes › Symfony bundle › `#[AsPrismListener]`
sections.content:
`Prism\Bundle\Attribute\AsPrismListener`: listens to a Prism event (`PrePersistEvent`, `PostFlushEvent`...). On a class (its `__invoke()` method) or a method; repeatable.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | `null` | The event class. `null`: the type of the method's first parameter |
| `method` | `null` | On a class: the method to call. `null`: `__invoke` |
| `entityManager` | `null` | The entity manager whose events are listened to. `null`: all of them |
| `priority` | `0` | Higher priorities run first |

sections.title: Attributes › Symfony bundle › `#[AsEntityListener]`
sections.content: `Prism\Bundle\Attribute\AsEntityListener`: makes an entity listener, named in `#[EntityListeners]`, a service with its dependencies. Without it, the listener is created without arguments. No parameter.

sections.title: Attributes › Symfony bundle › `#[AsEmbeddingProvider]`
sections.content:
`Prism\Bundle\Attribute\AsEmbeddingProvider`: registers an `EmbeddingProvider` service under a name, the one `#[EmbeddedVector(model:)]` gives. Without it, an autoconfigured provider is registered under its service id. See [Embeddings](/bundle/symfony#embeddings).

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `'default'` | The name of the provider |

sections.title: Attributes › Symfony bundle › `#[MapEntity]`
sections.content:
`Prism\Bundle\Attribute\MapEntity`: how a controller argument typed with an entity is loaded from the route. Without it, the identifier is the route parameter named after the argument, or `{id}`.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `null` | The route parameter that holds the identifier |
| `mapping` | `null` | Route parameter → field, looked up with `findOneBy()`: `['number' => 'number']` |
| `entityManager` | `null` | The entity manager. `null`: the first one that maps the class |
| `disabled` | `false` | Leaves the argument to the other value resolvers |

sections.title: Attributes › Migrations › `#[IgnoreLint]`
sections.content:
`Prism\Migrations\Lint\IgnoreLint`: silences one linter rule for a migration. Class attribute, repeatable.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | | The rule, `'L12'` for example |
| `reason` | | Why the case is accepted; required, and shown by `db:migrations:lint` |

sections.title: Attributes › Test pack › `#[WithRealTransactions]`
sections.content: `Prism\TestPack\Attribute\WithRealTransactions`: on a test class or method that uses `ResetDatabase`, disables the surrounding transaction: commits are real, and the schema is created again after the test. For a test that reads from another connection, or runs DDL under MySQL and MariaDB. No parameter.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.content:
Every option of `config/packages/prism.yaml`. An unknown option is refused when the container compiles, with a message that names it. This page is checked against the configuration tree of the bundle.

The complete form, with the default values:

```yaml
prism:
    default_entity_manager: ~             # the first declared entity manager
    connections:
        default:
            url: '%env(resolve:DATABASE_URL)%'
    entity_managers:
        default:
            connection: ~                 # the connection with the same name, or the only one
            entity_dirs: ['%kernel.project_dir%/src/Entity']
            batch_size: 100
            migrations:
                dir: ~                    # migrations/, or migrations/<Name> for another entity manager
                namespace: ~              # App\Migrations, or App\Migrations\<Name>
    connection_idle_ttl: 60
    tenancy:
        type: integer
        guard: ~                          # exception in debug, log otherwise
        resolver: ~                       # one of header, subdomain, user
        loader: ~
    embeddings:
        scheduler: auto                   # messenger if a message bus exists, deferred otherwise
        batch_size: 64
        providers: {}                     # <name>: { service: … } or { openai: { … } }
    metamodel:
        dir: '%kernel.cache_dir%/prism/metamodel'
```

sections.title: Configuration › Short form
sections.content:
With one database and one entity manager, `url`, `entity_dirs` and `migrations` can be written at the root. They declare the `default` connection and entity manager, and cannot be mixed with `connections` and `entity_managers`.

```yaml
prism:
    url: '%env(resolve:DATABASE_URL)%'
    entity_dirs: ['%kernel.project_dir%/src/Entity']
    migrations:
        dir: '%kernel.project_dir%/migrations'
        namespace: 'App\Migrations'
```

sections.title: Configuration › Short form › `prism.url`
sections.content: The URL of the `default` connection. Without `url` and `connections`, Prism uses `%env(resolve:DATABASE_URL)%`, read on first use only.

sections.title: Configuration › Short form › `prism.entity_dirs`
sections.content: The entity directories of the `default` entity manager.

sections.title: Configuration › Short form › `prism.migrations.dir`
sections.content: The migrations directory of the `default` entity manager.

sections.title: Configuration › Short form › `prism.migrations.namespace`
sections.content: The namespace of its migrations.

sections.title: Configuration › Connections › `prism.connections.<name>.url`
sections.content: The URL of a named connection, in Symfony's format, with `serverVersion`: `mysql://user:pass@host:3306/db?serverVersion=8.4`. Required.

sections.title: Configuration › Entity managers › `prism.default_entity_manager`
sections.content: The entity manager behind `EntityManagerInterface` and `bin/console db:*` without `--em`. Default: the first declared.

sections.title: Configuration › Entity managers › `prism.entity_managers.<name>.connection`
sections.content: The connection of the entity manager. Default: the connection with the same name, or the only connection if there is one.

sections.title: Configuration › Entity managers › `prism.entity_managers.<name>.entity_dirs`
sections.content: The directories of its entity classes, at least one. Default: `%kernel.project_dir%/src/Entity`.

sections.title: Configuration › Entity managers › `prism.entity_managers.<name>.batch_size`
sections.content: The largest number of entities loaded by one `IN` query of [batch fetching](/guide/n-plus-one#batch-size), at least 1. Default: `100`. A relation can set its own with `batchSize`.

sections.title: Configuration › Entity managers › `prism.entity_managers.<name>.migrations.dir`
sections.content: Its migrations directory. Default: `%kernel.project_dir%/migrations` for the default entity manager, `migrations/<Name>` for the others.

sections.title: Configuration › Entity managers › `prism.entity_managers.<name>.migrations.namespace`
sections.content: The namespace of its migrations. Default: `App\Migrations`, or `App\Migrations\<Name>`.

sections.title: Configuration › Worker mode › `prism.connection_idle_ttl`
sections.content: Under FrankenPHP or RoadRunner: after this many seconds without a query, the connection is checked at the start of the next request, and reconnected if it was lost. `0` checks it on every request. Default: `60`.

sections.title: Configuration › Multi-tenancy
sections.content: See [Multi-tenancy](/guide/multi-tenancy#in-symfony).

sections.title: Configuration › Multi-tenancy › `prism.tenancy.type`
sections.content: The type of the `tenant_id` column of every `#[Tenanted]` entity: `integer`, `bigint` or `uuid`. Default: `integer`.

sections.title: Configuration › Multi-tenancy › `prism.tenancy.guard`
sections.content: What the guard does with raw SQL on a tenanted table without a tenant condition: `exception`, or `log` (a critical log entry). Default: `exception` in debug, `log` otherwise.

sections.title: Configuration › Multi-tenancy › `prism.tenancy.resolver.header`
sections.content: Read the tenant from this request header, `X-Tenant-Id` for example. Before the firewall. **Only behind a gateway that sets the header itself**: otherwise, any client chooses its tenant.

sections.title: Configuration › Multi-tenancy › `prism.tenancy.resolver.subdomain`
sections.content: Read the tenant from the subdomain under this domain: `acme` in `acme.example.com` under `example.com`. Before the firewall.

sections.title: Configuration › Multi-tenancy › `prism.tenancy.resolver.user`
sections.content:
`true`: the tenant of the logged-in user, which implements `TenantAwareUserInterface`. After the firewall; the user entity must not be tenanted.

Only one of `header`, `subdomain` and `user` can be set. Without any, the application sets the tenant on the `StackTenantContext` service.

sections.title: Configuration › Multi-tenancy › `prism.tenancy.loader`
sections.content: The id of a `TenantLoader` service that turns the identifier read by the resolver (a header value, a subdomain) into the tenant identifier. Without it, the identifier read is the tenant, an integer for `integer` and `bigint`.

sections.title: Configuration › Embeddings
sections.content: The providers and the computation of the `#[EmbeddedVector]` fields. See [Embeddings](../symfony.md#embeddings).

sections.title: Configuration › Embeddings › `prism.embeddings.scheduler`
sections.content: What happens to the vectors a flush made stale, once its transaction is committed: `messenger` dispatches `ComputeEmbedding` messages, `synchronous` computes them at once, `deferred` leaves them to `db:embeddings:compute`. Default: `auto`, which is `messenger` when a message bus exists, `deferred` otherwise. `messenger` without a bus is refused.

sections.title: Configuration › Embeddings › `prism.embeddings.batch_size`
sections.content: The texts sent to a provider in one call, the ids in one `ComputeEmbedding` message, and the messages the handler processes together. Default: `64`.

sections.title: Configuration › Embeddings › `prism.embeddings.providers.<name>.service`
sections.content: The id of a service that implements `EmbeddingProvider`, registered under `<name>`: the name that `#[EmbeddedVector(model:)]` gives. A provider is either `service` or `openai`.

sections.title: Configuration › Embeddings › `prism.embeddings.providers.<name>.openai.base_url`
sections.content: The base URL of an API in the OpenAI format, without `/embeddings`: `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `http://ollama:11434/v1`. Needs `prism-orm/embedding-openai` and `symfony/http-client`.

sections.title: Configuration › Embeddings › `prism.embeddings.providers.<name>.openai.model`
sections.content: The model sent with each request, and stored with each vector it computes.

sections.title: Configuration › Embeddings › `prism.embeddings.providers.<name>.openai.dimensions`
sections.content: The dimension of its vectors. It must equal the `dimensions` of the column, checked at `cache:warmup`, and every response is checked against it.

sections.title: Configuration › Embeddings › `prism.embeddings.providers.<name>.openai.api_key`
sections.content: The API key, sent as a bearer token. `~` for a local server. Use an environment variable: `'%env(OPENAI_API_KEY)%'`.

sections.title: Configuration › Embeddings › `prism.embeddings.providers.<name>.openai.send_dimensions`
sections.content: `true` sends the dimension with each request, for the models that reduce it (`text-embedding-3-*`). Default: `false`.

sections.title: Configuration › Embeddings › `prism.embeddings.providers.<name>.openai.prefix`
sections.content: Put before each text. Some models expect a prefix that tells documents from questions: `'search_document: '` and `'search_query: '` for `nomic-embed-text`, as two providers of the same model. Default: `''`.

sections.title: Configuration › Metamodel › `prism.metamodel.dir`
sections.content: The directory of the generated [metamodel](/guide/query-builder#the-metamodel); each entity manager generates into `<dir>/<name>`. Default: `%kernel.cache_dir%/prism/metamodel`.

sections.title: PHPStan errors
sections.content: The errors reported by Prism's [PHPStan extension](/guide/phpstan), by identifier. Each identifier can be ignored in your PHPStan configuration like any other, although each one points at code that fails at run time.

sections.title: PHPStan errors › Repository calls
sections.content: These rules check the criteria and order arguments of `findBy()`, `findOneBy()`, `count()`, `iterate()`, `nearest()` and `hybridSearch()` on a Prism repository, and the field that `nearest()` searches.

sections.title: PHPStan errors › Repository calls › `prism.findBy.unknownField`
sections.content:
A key of the criteria or of the order is not a field of the entity.

```text
Unknown field App\Entity\Customer::$emial in the criteria of findBy(). Did you mean "email"?
```

```php no-run
$customers->findBy(['emial' => 'ada@example.test']);
```

**Fix:** use the property name of the entity, not the column name: `['email' => ...]`. The suggestion is the closest field name.

sections.title: PHPStan errors › Repository calls › `prism.findBy.relation`
sections.content:
A key designates a collection, or the inverse side of a relation: neither has a column to compare.

```text
App\Entity\Customer::$orders is a collection: findBy() compares only fields and owning ToOne relations; join it with the typed query builder instead.
```

```php no-run
$customers->findBy(['orders' => $order]);
```

**Fix:** compare from the owning side (`$orders->findBy(['customer' => $customer])`), or join the relation in a [typed query](/guide/query-builder#joins).

sections.title: PHPStan errors › Repository calls › `prism.findBy.invalidOrder`
sections.content:
A value of the order argument is not a case of `Prism\Dbal\Query\Order`.

```text
The order of App\Entity\Customer::$name in findBy() is 'ASC', not a Prism\Dbal\Query\Order case.
```

```php no-run
$customers->findBy([], ['name' => 'ASC']);
```

**Fix:** `['name' => Order::Asc]`, with `use Prism\Dbal\Query\Order;`.

sections.title: PHPStan errors › Repository calls › `prism.nearest.notVector`
sections.content:
The field searched by `nearest()` is not a field of type `vector` of the entity. The message lists the vector fields the entity has.

```text
App\Entity\Article::$title is not a vector field: nearest() searches a field of type "vector" (embedding).
```

```php no-run
$articles->nearest('title', $question);
```

**Fix:** name the vector field, here `'embedding'`.

sections.title: PHPStan errors › Projections
sections.content: These rules check the named arguments of `selectInto(Dto::class, ...)` against the constructor of the DTO, as Prism does before running the query.

sections.title: PHPStan errors › Projections › `prism.selectInto.unnamed`
sections.content:
A selection is passed without a name.

```text
Each selection of selectInto(App\Report\CustomerRevenue::class, ...) is named after a parameter of its constructor, such as total: $o->total->sum().
```

```php no-run
$query->selectInto(CustomerRevenue::class, $c->name, $i->total->sum());
```

**Fix:** name each selection after the constructor parameter it fills: `customer: $c->name, total: $i->total->sum()`.

sections.title: PHPStan errors › Projections › `prism.selectInto.unknownParameter`
sections.content:
A selection is named after no parameter of the constructor.

```text
The selection "amount" matches no parameter of App\Report\CustomerRevenue::__construct() (customer, invoices, total, lastInvoice).
```

```php no-run
$query->selectInto(CustomerRevenue::class, customer: $c->name, amount: $i->total->sum());
```

**Fix:** use one of the parameter names listed in the message.

sections.title: PHPStan errors › Projections › `prism.selectInto.missingParameter`
sections.content:
A required parameter of the constructor is not selected.

```text
The parameter $lastInvoice of App\Report\CustomerRevenue::__construct() is required but not selected: select it as lastInvoice: ...
```

**Fix:** select it, or give the parameter a default value in the DTO.

sections.title: PHPStan errors › Projections › `prism.selectInto.typeMismatch`
sections.content:
A selection has a type that its parameter does not accept.

```text
The selection "total" is string|null, but $total of App\Report\CustomerRevenue::__construct() accepts string.
```

**Fix:** align the parameter with the selection. An aggregate other than `count()` is `null` on an empty set, so its parameter is nullable: `?string $total`. A `decimal` is a `string`, never a `float`.

sections.title: Events
sections.content:
Prism publishes typed PSR-14 events through the event dispatcher of each entity manager. In Symfony, listen to them with [`#[AsPrismListener]`](/reference/attributes#asprismlistener); without Symfony, pass any PSR-14 dispatcher to the `EntityManager`:

```php no-run
$em = new EntityManager($connection, $metadata, events: $dispatcher);
```

For the events of one entity class, [lifecycle callbacks](/guide/mapping#lifecycle-callbacks) on the entity or [entity listeners](/reference/attributes#entitylisteners) are simpler: they receive the entity directly.

All events are in `Prism\Orm\Event`, except `NPlusOneDetected`, in `Prism\Orm\Debug`. Their properties are `readonly`.

The `unitOfWork` property of an event is a `Prism\Orm\UnitOfWork\FlushContext`: what a listener may see and do during a flush. It lists the entities to insert, update and delete (`getScheduledInsertions()`, `getScheduledUpdates()`, `getScheduledDeletions()`), tells whether anything would be written (`hasPendingChanges()`), gives the state of an entity (`contains()`, `getEntityState()`), and accepts `persist()` and `remove()` from `PreFlushEvent` or `OnFlushEvent`, which this same flush then writes. The rest of the unit of work is internal to Prism.

sections.title: Events › Flush
sections.content: A flush publishes `PreFlushEvent` and `OnFlushEvent` before its transaction, `PrePersistEvent` and `PreUpdateEvent` for each entity inside it, then after the commit `PostPersistEvent`, `PostUpdateEvent`, `PostRemoveEvent` and `AuditRecordedEvent`, and `PostFlushEvent` last. If the flush fails, nothing is published after the rollback. Calling `flush()` from a listener throws `ReentrantFlushException`.

sections.title: Events › Flush › `PreFlushEvent`
sections.content:
At the start of `flush()`, before any change is computed: an entity persisted or modified here is written by this flush.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Flush › `OnFlushEvent`
sections.content:
The changes are computed, before the transaction starts. `FlushContext::getScheduled*()` lists them; a change made here is included.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Flush › `PrePersistEvent`
sections.content:
Before the `INSERT` of an entity, in the transaction of the flush; a change to the entity is inserted.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` | `object` | The entity |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Flush › `PreUpdateEvent`
sections.content:
Before the `UPDATE` of an entity; a change to the entity is included, and only that entity's changeset is computed again.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` | `object` | The entity |
| `changeSet` | `array<string, array{mixed, mixed}>` | Field → [old value, new value] |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Flush › `PostPersistEvent`
sections.content:
After the commit of the flush that inserted the entity, never inside its transaction.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` | `object` | The entity, with its generated identifier |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Flush › `PostUpdateEvent`
sections.content:
After the commit of the flush that updated the entity.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` | `object` | The entity |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Flush › `PostRemoveEvent`
sections.content:
After the commit of the flush that deleted the entity.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` | `object` | The entity |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Flush › `AuditRecordedEvent`
sections.content:
The audit rows written by a flush, published after its commit. The Audit panel of the Symfony profiler listens to it; listen to it to copy the log elsewhere.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entries` | `list<AuditEntry>` | One entry per audited entity changed |

sections.title: Events › Flush › `PostFlushEvent`
sections.content:
After the commit and the other `Post*` events; never after a failure.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Flush › `InverseSideChangedEvent`
sections.content:
At flush, a collection on the inverse side of a relation changed without its owning side: nothing is written for that change. An added element does not point to the owner, or a removed one still does. The Symfony bundle logs it as a warning in development.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | `object` | The entity whose collection changed |
| `field` | `string` | The collection property |
| `element` | `object` | The element added or removed |
| `added` | `bool` | `true` if added, `false` if removed |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Entities › `PreRemoveEvent`
sections.content:
When `remove()` is called, before the entity is scheduled for deletion.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` | `object` | The entity |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Entities › `PostLoadEvent`
sections.content:
After an entity is loaded from the database: `find()`, `findBy()`, `iterate()`, a reference that loads, `refresh()`. Never for an entity that the identity map returns.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` | `object` | The entity |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Entities › `OnClearEvent`
sections.content:
After `clear()`: every entity is detached.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Diagnostics › `BatchLoadedEvent`
sections.content:
A batch load: one query for a whole cohort. Published only when the batch holds at least two entities; the Symfony profiler shows them.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entityClass` | `class-string` | Without `association`: the class of the entities loaded together. With it: the class of the owners |
| `association` | `?string` | `null` for referenced entities loaded together; otherwise the relation loaded for the owners (a collection, or the inverse side of a `OneToOne`) |
| `count` | `int` | The number of entities, or of owners |
| `unitOfWork` | `FlushContext` | |

sections.title: Events › Diagnostics › `NPlusOneDetected`
sections.content:
`Prism\Orm\Debug\NPlusOneDetected`, published by the [N+1 detector](/guide/n-plus-one#the-n-1-detector) when the same read query ran more times than its threshold since its last `reset()`. Published once per query.

| Property | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sql` | `string` | The normalized SQL: values and `IN` lists replaced by `?` |
| `count` | `int` | How many times it ran |
| `origin` | `string` | `file:line` of the first frame outside `vendor/` and Prism: the line of your code that started the loop |

sections.title: Exceptions
sections.content:
Every exception that Prism throws implements `Prism\Exception\PrismException`, and an interface per package: `DbalException`, `OrmException`, `MigrationsException`, `BundleException`. Catch one of them to handle all the errors of a package.

The messages are in English and name what is concerned: the entity, the field, the identifier, the table. They never contain a bound value or a password, which may be sensitive.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM
sections.content: `Prism\Orm\Exception`, package `prism-orm/orm`.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `MappingException`
sections.content:
A mapping attribute has an invalid argument, or the mapping of an entity is invalid: no identifier, a `\DateTime` property, a contradiction between `nullable` and the PHP type, a relation whose other side does not match... The message lists every error with its class and field.

**Fix:** follow the message; `db:schema:validate` lists all the errors of all the entities at once.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `InvalidEntityStateException`
sections.content:
An operation that the state of the entity does not allow: `remove()` on a new entity, `persist()` on a detached one, for example.

**Fix:** see the [entity states](/guide/entity-manager#entity-states). A detached entity is loaded again with `find()`.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `UnpersistedRelationException`
sections.content:
At flush, a new entity is reachable through a relation of a managed one, but was never persisted. The message gives the entity, the field and the path. Nothing was written.

**Fix:** `persist()` it, or add `cascade: [Prism\Cascade::Persist]` to the relation.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `CyclicDependencyException`
sections.content:
The `INSERT` statements of a flush cannot be ordered: the entities reference each other in a cycle in which no foreign key is nullable.

**Fix:** make one foreign key of the cycle nullable. Prism then inserts it as `NULL` and sets it with an `UPDATE` afterwards.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `ReentrantFlushException`
sections.content:
`flush()` was called during a flush, from an event listener or a lifecycle callback.

**Fix:** change entities in `PreFlushEvent`, `OnFlushEvent` or `PreUpdateEvent`, which the running flush writes; or flush after it returns.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `OrphanReattachedException`
sections.content:
An entity removed from a collection with `orphanRemoval` was attached to another parent in the same flush, while it is going to be deleted.

**Fix:** flush the removal first, or move the entity without `orphanRemoval`.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `EntityNotFoundException`
sections.content:
The row of an entity does not exist, or not anymore: a reference that loads, `refresh()`, `lock()`. The message gives the class and the identifier.

**Fix:** use `find()`, which returns `null`, when the row may be missing.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `OptimisticLockException`
sections.content:
The row changed since it was loaded: the `UPDATE` or `DELETE` checked against the [`#[Version]`](/reference/attributes#version) field matched no row. Also thrown by an optimistic `lock()` on an outdated version, or on an entity without a version.

**Fix:** load the entity again and reapply the change, or tell the user that someone else changed it.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `TransactionRequiredException`
sections.content:
A pessimistic `lock()` outside a transaction.

**Fix:** call it inside `wrapInTransaction()`.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `NonUniqueResultException`
sections.content:
`getOneOrNull()` on a query that returns several entities.

**Fix:** add a condition, or use `getResult()` or `limit(1)`.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `QueryException`
sections.content:
A typed query is invalid: an alias that is not part of the query, a stale metamodel, a fetch join of an alias that is not fetched, a `limit()` with a fetch-joined collection, an entity query with a `groupBy()`, a selected field that is not grouped, a `selectInto()` that does not match its DTO, an invalid JSON path, a pagination without order or with a `limit()`.

**Fix:** follow the message. PHPStan reports the `selectInto()` cases during analysis; in development, a stale metamodel is regenerated when the kernel boots.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `InvalidArgumentException`
sections.content:
An argument refused by an ORM API: a batch size out of range, a criterion that holds an unsaved entity, a filter name that already exists or does not, the tenant filter disabled, `restore()` on an entity that is not soft-deletable.

**Fix:** follow the message.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `MetamodelException`
sections.content:
The metamodel cannot be written in its directory.

**Fix:** make the directory writable, or choose another one (`metamodel.dir`, `--dir`).

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `VectorDimensionMismatchException`
sections.content:
At flush, a vector has more or fewer components than the `dimensions` of its column. The message gives the entity, the field and both dimensions. Nothing was written.

**Fix:** store the output of the embedding model the column was created for. A different model needs a new column size, or a migration.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `EmbeddingException`
sections.content:
An `#[EmbeddedVector]` could not be computed: its provider name is not registered, the provider failed (network, quota), or it returned the wrong number of vectors or the wrong dimension. The rows stay stale, left out of `nearest()`. A `ComputeEmbedding` message is retried.

**Fix:** register the provider under the name the attribute gives (`model: 'default'`), and check that its dimension is the one of the column. Then run `db:embeddings:compute`.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `MissingTenantException`
sections.content:
An operation on a `#[Tenanted]` entity without a current tenant. Prism has no implicit "all tenants" mode.

**Fix:** set the tenant (`setTenantId()`, `runAs()`), or use `runAsSystem()` for an operation on every tenant. See [Multi-tenancy](/guide/multi-tenancy#no-tenant-no-query).

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `TenantMismatchException`
sections.content:
The tenant property of an entity holds another tenant than the current one, or was changed: the tenant of a row never changes.

**Fix:** let Prism fill the tenant property; to create an entity for another tenant, do it inside `runAs()`.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `CrossTenantRelationException`
sections.content:
At flush, a relation links two tenanted entities of different tenants. Refused even in system mode.

**Fix:** link entities of the same tenant; a shared reference row belongs to an entity marked `#[Tenanted(global: true)]`.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `TenantSwitchException`
sections.content:
The tenant changed while the unit of work had unsaved changes. When entering `runAs()` or `runAsSystem()`, the switch is refused and nothing is lost; when leaving, the changes made inside are discarded, never written under another tenant.

**Fix:** flush before entering, and before leaving.

sections.title: Exceptions › ORM › `UnfilteredTenantQueryException`
sections.content:
Raw SQL on a tenanted table without a condition on its tenant column, a `TRUNCATE`, or SQL that the guard cannot analyze. Thrown by the tenant guard in `exception` mode.

**Fix:** add `tenant_id = ?` to the `WHERE` or `ON` of each tenanted table, or run the query in `runAsSystem()` if it really concerns every tenant. See [Raw SQL](/guide/multi-tenancy#raw-sql).

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL
sections.content: `Prism\Dbal\Exception`, package `prism-orm/dbal`.

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `ConnectionFailedException`
sections.content:
The database connection could not be opened.

**Fix:** check the host, the credentials and that the server runs; the message is the driver's.

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `InvalidUrlException`
sections.content:
The database URL cannot be read or is incomplete. The password never appears in the message.

**Fix:** use Symfony's format, `driver://user:pass@host:port/db?serverVersion=x`.

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `UnsupportedPlatformException`
sections.content:
The `serverVersion` cannot be read, or is older than what Prism supports: MySQL 8.0, MariaDB 11.8, PostgreSQL 15, SQLite 3.40.

**Fix:** set `serverVersion` to the real version of the server, which must be supported.

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `QueryFailedException`
sections.content:
The server refused a query. The exception carries the SQL and the SQLSTATE, never the bound values.

**Fix:** read the SQLSTATE: a constraint violation, a missing table (run the migrations), a syntax error in your own SQL.

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `AbortedTransactionException`
sections.content:
Under PostgreSQL, a failed query invalidated the transaction: a `COMMIT` would silently become a `ROLLBACK`. Prism rolls back and says so.

**Fix:** handle the first failure; to continue a transaction after an expected failure, run the risky query inside a nested transaction (a savepoint).

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `NoActiveTransactionException`
sections.content:
`commit()` or `rollBack()` without an open transaction, or after MySQL or MariaDB committed it implicitly with a DDL statement.

**Fix:** pair each `beginTransaction()` with one `commit()` or `rollBack()`, or use `transactional()`.

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `ConversionException`
sections.content:
A value cannot be converted between PHP and the database: a `float` for a `decimal`, a mutable `\DateTime`, a number with more significant digits than the column holds, invalid JSON... The message names the type and the expected form, never the value.

**Fix:** pass the PHP type of the column: a `string` for a `decimal`, a `\DateTimeImmutable` for a date.

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `InvalidParameterException`
sections.content:
A value that cannot be bound (not a scalar), positional and named parameters mixed, an invalid savepoint name or JSON path.

**Fix:** follow the message.

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `InvalidQueryException`
sections.content:
A query of the DBAL query builder is inconsistent: a clause that this kind of query does not allow, no table, an empty `SELECT` or `IN` list, a comparison with `null` (use `isNull()`).

**Fix:** follow the message.

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `InvalidIdentifierException`
sections.content:
A table, column or index name that cannot be quoted safely on the platform: empty, with invalid characters, or too long.

**Fix:** rename it.

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `InvalidSchemaException`
sections.content:
A schema object is inconsistent, or cannot be translated into DDL on the platform: a duplicate or unknown column, a nullable primary key, a foreign key to an unknown table, a type or feature the platform does not support.

**Fix:** follow the message; it names the table and the column.

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `UnknownTypeException`
sections.content:
A column type that is not registered in the `TypeRegistry`.

**Fix:** check the name, or register the custom type (in Symfony, tag it `prism.type`).

sections.title: Exceptions › DBAL › `DuplicateTypeException`
sections.content:
A type registered twice under the same name.

**Fix:** choose another name for the custom type.

sections.title: Exceptions › Migrations
sections.content: `Prism\Migrations\Exception`, package `prism-orm/migrations`.

sections.title: Exceptions › Migrations › `MigrationException`
sections.content:
A migration cannot run: an invalid file name, a missing class, a class that is not a migration, an unknown version, a migration already executed or not executed, a migration modified after it ran, an invalid operation, or a failure while it ran.

**Fix:** follow the message. For a migration modified after it ran, restore it, or run `migrate --allow-modified` if the change is deliberate.

sections.title: Exceptions › Migrations › `IrreversibleMigrationException`
sections.content:
The `down()` of a migration that cannot be reverted: it has none, or reverting it would need data that it destroyed.

**Fix:** none in the general case; restore a backup, or write a `down()` if the data can be rebuilt.

sections.title: Exceptions › Symfony bundle
sections.content: `Prism\Bundle\Exception`, package `prism-orm/bundle`.

sections.title: Exceptions › Symfony bundle › `InvalidConfigurationException`
sections.content:
`prism.yaml` is inconsistent: short and complete forms mixed, an entity manager whose connection is not declared, an unknown default entity manager.

**Fix:** follow the message; see the [configuration reference](/reference/configuration).

sections.title: Exceptions › Symfony bundle › `MapEntityException`
sections.content:
`#[MapEntity]` is misused: an unknown entity manager, a missing route parameter, a field that does not exist. A programming error, never a 404.

**Fix:** follow the message.

sections.title: Exceptions › Symfony bundle › `MakerException`
sections.content:
`make:entity` or `make:migration` cannot complete: a file it cannot read, a missing class.

**Fix:** follow the message.

sections.title: Exceptions › Test pack › `TestPackException`
sections.content:
`Prism\TestPack\Exception\TestPackException`: the test pack is misused, for example a factory used before the kernel boots, an unknown attribute, or queries counted while they are not recorded. A test error, never an application one.

**Fix:** follow the message.
